parties:
Nazir Ahmed & others ------ Appellants 
-Versus-
Md. Fajal Ahmed & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The plaintiffs brought the suit stating inter alia that some 1.13 acres of land covered by two S.S. plots namely, 2088 and 2007 appertaining to Khatian No. 1220 of Mouza Kumargoan J.L. No. 18 originally belonged to Jogendra Mohantha and Mahananda Mahantha sons of Paramananda Mahantha who having been khas possession of the suit land sold the same in favour of Rosomoy Chandra by a registered kabala dated 16.06.1960; while Rosomoy Chandra was in possession and enjoyment of the suit land the same was put to auction owing to non payment of rent and eventually Certificate Case No. 188/64-65 was initiated and upon conclusion thereof the suit land was sold in auction in due process; Taheruddin purchased the suit land in the said auction held on 29.10.64 and the said sale was made absolute and certificate was issued in favour of Taheruddin on 20.01.1965; thereafter, Taheruddin sold the suit land in favour of Ershad Ali by a registered kabala dated 07.04.1975 who also sold the suit land to Raisa Bibi who got possession; thereafter Raisa Bibi being in possession of the suit land sold the same in favour of Tullai Bibi in the year 1979; thereafter Tullai having been in possession of the suit land got her name mutated in the record of rights and eventually she gifted away the suit land to her son Moklis Miah by a deed of gift dated 20.11.1986 and upon taking over possession of the suit land Moklis Miah got his name mutated in the record of rights in respect of the suit land; thereafter on 27.06.1992 Moklis Miah sold the suit land in favourt of plaintiff Fazal Ahmed and one Akbor Ali and had handed over possession; said Akbor Ali subsequently sold his part of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff Fazal Ahmed, thereafter the plaintiff got his exclusive title in the suit land in the manner aforesaid and also got possession thereof. 

 Thereafter, the plaintiff made an attempt to get his name mutated in respect of suit land but it was found that the names of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had already been recorded in respect of the suit land although they had no right, title, interest or possession therein and upon query the defendant No. 3 disclosed for the first time that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had purchased the suit land from Abul Hashem by a registered kabala dated 18.11.74 in the name of Chand Miah the defendant No. 1 and by another kabala dated 02.12.1974 in favour of defendant No. 2 Raja Miah; and defendant No. 3 made an attempt for sale of the suit land; thereafter the plaintiff got information about the three kabalas as disclosed above which are dated 30.03.1973, 18.11. 1974 and 02.12.1974; thus the cause of action arose and the suit was filed seeking redress. 

 5. In the process aforesaid the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 entered into possession of the entire suit land in exercise or their right and title they also got their names mutated in respect of the record of right. It is also asserted in the written statement that in view of setting aside of the sale in auction in the Certificate Case as aforesaid the registered sale deed in favour of Taheruddin in the Certificate Case was rendered invalid, therefore, subsequent purchases as claimed in the plaint from Taheruddin were also rendered invalid consequently they did not acquire any right, title, possession and interest in respect of their alleged purchased land. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are residents of London, therefore, they appointed one Manik Miah as their attorney empowering him to sell the suit land. The answering defendant Nos. 4-6 purchased the suit land from appointed attorney of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered kabala dated 22.05.98 at a consideration of Tk. 50,000/00 and after such purchase they have been in possession of the suit land in exercise of their right title and interest. 

 Referring to the evidence on record Mr. Mondal submits that the plaintiff utterly failed in substantiating his claim that the kabala dated 18.11.1974 and 2.12.74 are either forged or fabricated or sham paper transaction. Therefore, question of decree in favour of the plaintiff as claimed does not arise at all. On the contrary, the evidence adduced by the defendants in support of their case employ prove that they have indeed acquired right title interest and possession in the suit land, therefore, the suit ought to have been dismissed as a whole. 

 23. Defendant No. 4 figured as witness No. 1 for the defendants who deposed that defendants 5-6 are his co-sharers who filed written statement jointly upon being added as defendants and he is deposing on behalf of defendants 5-6 as well. He also testifies that Mohendra and Mohananda were the original owners of the suit land who having been in possession thereof sold the same in favour of Rosomoy by registered kabala dated 11.06.1960, thereafter Rosomoy Nath sold the suit land to Abdul Hashem by registered kabala. He also deposed that Sachindra son of Mohendra became the Sole heir of two Mohanthas. This witness also testifies that after purchase by Abdul Hashem it was detected that Taheruddin once purchased the suit land in auction though no notice either upon Rosomoy or Abdul Hashem was ever served, record of right was in favour of Mohendra and Mohantha and on the basis of such record of right certificate case was proceeded and the auction took place. It was also deposed that Abdul Hashem, Rosomoy and Sachindra jointly initiated Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 for setting aside the auction sale on the basis whereof, on 13.02.74 the auction sale was set aside. This witness also produced the certified copy of the order dated 13.02.74 passed in the said Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 and marked as Ext. Ka. This witness produced the certified copy of the application for setting aside the sale which has been marked as Ext. Kha. This witness testifies further that after setting aside the auction sale the subsequent title on purchase were rendered invalid, therefore, title of purchasers have extinguished and upon setting aside the action sale Abdul Hashem entered into possession of the suit land. Thereafter, Abdul Hashem sold the same in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered kabla in the year 1974. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 has been residing in London. Defendant No. 3 is the father of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 who is also a resident of London. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 executed a power of attorney for transfer of the suit land in favour of Manik Miah, the plaintiff wanted to purchase the suit land but he was not agreeable to pay the market price so he failed, therefore, Manik Miah sold the said land in favour of defendant Nos. 4-6 by a registered kabala dated 22.05.1988. This said document has been produced in the court and marked as Ext. Ga (with objection). This witness also testifies that he had purchased the suit land at a consideration of Tk. 5(five) lacs. The original deed of transfer was in custody of the seller so he handed over to the defendant Nos. 4-6 which has been produced before the court and marked as Ext. Ga-1. The registered sale deed dated 30.03.1973 executed by Rosomoy in favour of Abul Hashem has also been produced before the court and marked as Ext. Ga-2. Thereafter Abul Hashem sold a part of the suit land in favour of defendant No. 1 by a registered kabala dated 18.11.1974 which has been produced and marked as Ext. Ga-3. The said Abdul Hashem also sold other part of the suit land in favour of defendant No. 2 by a registered kabala dated 01.12.74 which has been produced and marked as Ext. Ga-4 after purchase the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 Chand Miah and Raja Miah got their names mutated in respect of the suit land being suit plot Nos. 2007 and 2088. This witness also produced the rent receipt evidencing payment of rent. This witness also testifies that the document in favour of the plaintiffs are collusive paper transaction which were never acted upon. 

 During cross-examination this witness admitted that he reside in a place eight miles away from the suit land while defendant No. 5 Imran Ahmed is a resident of a place 15-16 miles away. The defendant No. 6 Ashis Kapali reside at 3 miles away from the suit land and he had seen the suit land for the first time one or two months before the date of their purchase, and they had no knowledge about the same earlier. This witness also disclosed that he had no knowledge, about the case prior to his purchase. This witness also admitted that Akbor Ali is a resident of a place situated near to the suit land. This witness also disclose that Abdul Hashem is no more. This witness also claims that the information slip filed by the plaintiff is a collusive paper. This witness also admitted in his cross-examination that record of Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 has not been called for. This witness denied the suggestion that there was no case initiated for cancellation of the auction sale. This witness also denied the suggestion that their document of purchase is forged one. This witness expressed his ignorance as to whether any heirs of Abdul Hashem is alive. This witness testifies that the document by which the suit land was purchased from Mohendra and Mohantha, was handed over to Manik Miah who handed over the same to this witness. This witness denied the suggestion that Abdul Hashem obtained the custody of the said document by practicing fraud. 

 30. D.W.8. is Taheruddin the auctioned purchaser of the suit land from whom the plaintiff claims to have purchased the suit land by way of successive devolution on transfer, deposed to the effect that he knows the plaintiff Fazal Ahmed, Nazir Ahmed, the defendants and the suit land. He also testifies that he had purchased the suit land in auction held in the auctioned Certificate Case No. 188/64-65 and his purchase took place on 29.10.64, he received possession through papers and as a matter of fact he did not get possession of the suit land physically. He also disposed that he sold the suit land in favor of Ershad Ali. Thereafter he received the notice for correction of record of rights in the year 1973 but he did not turn up on receipt of the said notice, this witness also testifies that he was informed about the setting aside of the auction sale in the year 1974. Thereafter he did not take care of the suit land. 

 33. From the materials placed before us and on consideration of evidence on record including the Exts. We find that the plaintiffs made desperate attempts to show that the action sale in favour of Taheruddin in connection with Certificate Case No. 188/64-65 was never set aside, therefore, they produced three information slip which have been marked as Ext. 9, Ext.9 (Ka) and 9(Kha). On a perusal of these Exts. we find that the Assistant Commissioner of Land (A.0 Land) Sardar Sylhet in his information slip issued on 01.07.1998 disclosed that Miscellaneous Cases, in the year 1973-74 used to have been filed before the R.D.C. Sylhet, therefore, no further information could be detected by this information slip which is Ext.9. The other information slip issued by A.D.C. (Rev.) Sylhet shows that a question put to them as to whether the records of Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 were available in the said office or not. The answer was given by the officer as "1". This information slip obtained by the plaintiff and marked as Ext. 9 (Ka) is dated 09.08.98. It may be mentioned that we have already noticed from Ext.9 the information slip dated 01.07.98. That the record of the said Miscellaneous Case was available with the office of the R.D.0 not with the A.D.C. (Rev). The other information slip which is marked as Ext. 9(Kha) is dated 24.10.1988 obtained from the Officer-in-charge. Collectorate, Sylhet singed by the A.C. (Land) disclosing to the effect that in his office the record of Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 is not available. Banking upon these exts. the plaintiffs made an attempt to show that the very proceeding in Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 is non existent, therefore, the question of cancellation of sale in favour of Taheruddin does not arise but in appreciation of the aforesaid position disclosed by the plaintiffs we feel inclined to take notice of two Exts. marked as Ext. Ka and Kha. Certified copies of the order sheet of Miscellaneous Case dated 13.02.74 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74 and the application for setting aside sale wherefrom it is evident that Sachin Chandra Mohantha and others were the applidants while Taheruddin was the opposite party. These certified copies were issued as back as on 09.04.74 long before the institution of the instant suit in the year 1997 which clearly shows that it was owing to non service of notice upon Sachin Chandra Mohantha the only admitted heir of the admitted owners, the auction sale was set aside by the Certificate Officer in Miscellaneous Case No. 2/73-74. 

 41. Send down the lower court records with a copy of the judgment to the trial court forth with.

lawyer:
Md Nurul Amin with Md Azizul Haque Sikder, Advocates—For the Appellants.
Abdul Quayum with Md Selim Reza Chowdhury, Advocates—For the Respondents.
parties:
Hachina Begum and others ------ Plaintiff-Appellants
vs
Abdul Mannan and others ------ Defendant-Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in-short, are that the present appellants as plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 23 of 1978 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal imp leading the defendants for declaration of title on the averments that one Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was owner of the suit land appertaining to CS Dag Nos.1194 and 1195 of Mouza Charvaduria measuring about 17.33 acres of land, who took settlement by executing a registered kabuliyat in favour of the then Government on 7-11-21. At the time of taking settlement of the suit land Abdul Kader Mia was a seasonal but collector of khash mohal; that Abdul Kader Mia died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs while he was in service; that Abdul Kader Mia in connection with his service posted different station in which he assigned his full brother defendant No. 2 to look after the suit property; that the defendant No.  2 with ill motive got the suit land recorded in the name of the defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia in equal share, that is, 3 arenas 4 gandas share; that the preparation of RS Khatian in the name of defendant Nos. 1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia was collusive and without any legal basis; that on the basis of wrong RS Khatian, the SA Khatian has also been pre-pared wrongly in the name of the defendants and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land in which the defendant Nos. 1-4, in-fact, have no right, title or legal interest whatsoever; that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was the exclusive owner of the suit land, who used to possess the suit land through different bargadars on the basis of barga Kabuliyats and after the death of Abdul Kader Mia, the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land through different bargadars on payment of rent to the Government; that the plaintiffs demanded Nadabinama or Multiparty in respect of the suit land in which the defendants Nos.1-4 have not tile or interest whatsoever but the defendant Nos.1-4 refused to execute any Nadabi  Muktipatra in their favour in respect of the suit land on 27th poush, 1384 BS; that the preparation of the wrong record of rights have cast a cloud upon the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and hence, the suit for declaration of title. 

 3. The defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint con-tending, inter alia, that Abdul Latif, the father of defendant Nos. 1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia took settlement of the suit land in the benami of his eldest son Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs; that Abdul Latif, the predecessor of the defendants got the suit land recorded during the time of PS operation of the year 1925 in Khatian No. 34 in the name of Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs to maintain benami character; that Abdul Latif Mia was a forester under Khas Mohal, when he took settlement of the suit land in the benami of his minor son Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs; that Abdul Latif Mia during his life time was in possession of the suit property on payment of rent to the Government; that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a minor school going student during the RS operation of the years, 1925 and was in joint mess with his father Abdul Latif in the year 1925; that Abdul Kader Mia had no source of income to take settlement of the suit land and he never possessed the suit land before the death of his father Abdul Latif Mia; that the kabulyat dated 7-11-21 was executed and registered in the name of Abdul Kader Mia by false percolation; that Abdul Latif Mia died before RS operation and Abdul Kader Mia the predecessor of the plaintiffs used to look after the property of his father; that Abdul Kader Mia got the suit land recorded in the name of his 5(five) brothers. The daughters of Abdul Latif Mia relinquished their claim in the suit land and thereupon, the suit land was recorded in the name of 5(five) brothers including Abdul Kader Mia in equal share in which they are in possession; that the SA operation has also been made correctly in the name of the defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia in equal share; that the defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs are in possession in the suit property in equal share on payment of rent to the Government; that the RS and SA khatian have been correctly prepared in the name of defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in equal share; that the plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit property relating to the shares of defendant Nos.1-4 and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. The learned trial Judge on consideration of the materials on record by his judgment and decree dated 29-8-1980 (decree signed on 4-9-1980) dismissed the suit mainly on 3 (three) counts: (1) that the suit is hopelessly barred by law of limitation. (2) that Abdul Kader Mia took settlement of the suit land in the became of his eldest son Kader Mia, who was a minor as per his service book (Exhibit 9) and the evidence of PW 1. (3) that the suit is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession over the suit land. 

 8. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellants in the course of his argument has taken us through the impugned judgment and decree, deposition of witnesses, exhibits and other materials on record and then submits that the findings of the trial Court below that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs had no source of income at the time of execution of kabuliyat dated 7-11-21 (Exhibit l) while he was a school going boy, his father Abdul Latif Mia took settlement of the suit land in the benami of his eldest son Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs is perverse being contrary to the material evidence on record. He next submits that the trial Court below having failed to consider the vital aspects of the case that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs took settlement of the suit land from the then government on 7-11-21 and he executed and registered Kabuliyat in favour of landlord on 7-11-1921 and to prove the case the original Kabulyat was called for from the collector ate on 11-8-1979 vide order No. 27, Kabulyat was exhibited as Exhibit 1 and the settlement was acted upon vide Exhibit Nos. 1A-1G that is the chronological registered barga kabulyat which were given by abraders in favour of Abdul Kader Mia and in those deeds including Exhibit 1 the occupation of Abdul Kader has been consistently stated as service holder. He further submits that the trial Court without assigning any sound reason most illegally ignored all registered documents (exhibits "1 and 1A-1G series") which were produced from the custody of the plaintiffs and those documents are more than 30 years old documents and have strong presumptive value as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act. 

 9. Mr Md Nurul Amin, further submits that the finding of the trial Court on the point of limitation is totally perverse inasmuch as the plaintiff's suit is for simple declaration of title and the proposition of law is well settled that the limitation will start not from the date of publication of record of right, so long any dispute as to title and possession is not raised there is no reason to institute a suit and in the present case it is apparent from the record that the title of the plaintiffs was threatened in the year 1977 and the suit was filed in the year 1978 and therefore, the suit is not barred by limitation. He adds that the wrong record of right by itself does not constitute a ground of limitation, when the title is threatened or evasion only then the cause of action would arise but the trial Court below failed to appreciate this simple point of law. 

 10. Mr Nurul Amin, further submits that the findings of the trial Court on the point of possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land is not only against the weight of evidence on record also contrary to the well settled principle of law inasmuch. as admittedly in the present case the SA and RS record was prepared in the name of the defendants along with the name of the plaintiffs but the defendants never paid any rent to the Government, on the other hand, the PW 1, Hanif Miah used to pay rent to the Government regularly vide exhibit 2A-2F starting from 1954 to 1975 and those rent receipts are evidence of possession and the same should be used as collateral evidence of title. He further points out that the plaintiff-appellants by adducing sufficient evidence both oral and documentary have been successfully proved their right, title and possession over the suit land and on the other hand, the defendant could not show any scrap of paper in support of their title and possession in the suit land but the trial Court below without considering the vital and ancient documents namely exhibit 1 and 2 series mechanically dismissed the suit which resulted in the failure of justice. 

 12. Mr Md Nurul Amin, finally relying on the decision reported in 1 XP (AD) 73 submits that the original title deed is in the name of, Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiff-appellants and on the basis of that registered kabuliyat PS record was prepared in the name of Abdul Kader Mia but subsequently SA and RS record was prepared in the name of the defendants and in such situation the conflicting between kabala and khatian the earlier registered kabuliyat prevails over the subsequent record of rights in RS khatian and SA khatian. 

 13. Mr Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate on the other hand, appearing for the defendant respondents in the course of argument after placing the impugned judgment and decree submits that the trial Court below after discussion of the evidence on record rightly arrived at a finding that Abdul Latif Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendants settled the suit property in the name of his minor son Abdul Kader Mia because he was govt. servant and it was possessed by Abdul Latif Mia during his life time and later on, his five sons possessed equally and accordingly RS and SA khatian was prepared in the name of five brothers at the instance of Abdul Kader Mia himself and all of them used to pay rent jointly. Mr Abdul Quayum, next submits that the learned Subordinate Judge, Barisal after discussion of the evidence on record rightly dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 29-8-1980 on the findings that the suit is barred by limitation and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a minor as per statement of PW 1 admitted is his evidence that his father was a student of Class X in 1925 in BM School as well as the service book of Abdul Kader Mia (Exhibit 9) shows his date of birth in 1904 and the suit is barred under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiffs do not have exclusive possession over the suit land. Mr Abdul Quayum, further submits that the plaintiffs tried to establish that the kabulyat dated 7-11-1921 is a registered document and the original was called for vide order No. 27 dated 11-8-1979 but there is no order or arrival of such record and there is nothing on record to show that registered kabulyat was produced before the Court below rather the kabulyat marked as "Exhibit 1" is an unregistered kabulyat and it was not proved by any manner as provided in the Evidence Act whatsoever. 

 14. He further upon placing the written objection filed by the only contesting defendant No.  2 and the evidence of DWs submits that the contesting defendant No. 2 pleaded that their father Abdul Latif Mia was a Government servant so he took settlement in the benami of his minor son from his own fund and possessed the same and after his death his 5 sons used to possess it and accordingly it has been recorded in RS and SA khatian and in that view of the matter the intention, motive and source of money, possession dealing with, preparation of RoR all the ingredients of benami transaction has been proved by the defendants by adducing evidence both oral and documentary. 

 16. We have heard the learned Advocates for both the sides at length and perused the evidence and materials on record including the impugned judgment and deposition of witnesses. Now, in order to resolve the disputes, let us examine first how far the learned Subordinate Judge was justified to dismiss the suit on the findings that Abdul Kader, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a benamder and the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession over the suit land. 

 23. In view of the above evidence both oral and documentary there is nothing on record to suggest that the plaintiffs are not in possession. Rather, the exhibited rent receipts and registered deeds in respect of the suit land demonstrate that the possession of plaintiff-appellants in the suit land. 

 24. In consideration of this material evidence on record and facts, our view is there-fore, that the reasons given by the trial Court below for passing the impugned judgment on the point that Abdul Kuader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a benamder and the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession over the suit land are not sustainable either in law or on facts. Furthermore, in his connection it may be mentioned that a kabuliyat (Exhibit 1) executed and registered in 1921 creates a presumption that the registration authority under the then British Government was satisfied that the executants Abdul Kader Mia was squarely a valid citizen to execute the kabuliyat (Exhibit 1). 

 26. We have already indicated that in view of the evidence both oral and documentary on the point of possession there is nothing on record to suggest that the plaintiffs are not in possession. PW 1, Hanif Miah used to pay rent to the Government regularly vide exhibit 2A to 2F starting from 1954-1975 and those rent receipts are evidence of possession. On examination of the rent receipts vide exhibit 2A to 2F together with the evidence of PWs and DWs. We are unable to agree with the finding of the trial Court that the suit was barred by law of limitation as well as barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession in the suit land within 12 years from before the date of filing of the suit. This finding of the trial Court below appears to be perverse and the same does not deserve to be sustained. 

 27. The proposition of law is well settled that the limitation will start not from the date of publication of record of right, so long any dispute as to title and possession is not raised and in the present case it is found from the record that the title of the plaintiffs was threatened in the year 1977 and the suit has been filed in 1978 and thus, the suit is not barred by limitation. Mr Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate in the facts and circumstance of the case rightly pointed out that the wrong record of right by itself does not constitute a ground of limitation, when the title is threatened or evasion only then the cause of action would arise but the trial Court below having failed to appreciate this simple point of law. We are inclined to agree with Mr Nurul Amin. 

 29. To meet the last branch of argument of Mr Abdul Quayum, we have carefully examined the entire evidence on record and it appears that at the trial both the parties admitted in their respective testimony that Exhibit 1, kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921 executed and registered by Abdul Kader Mia. It also appears that out of 4 defendants only defendant No.  2 (DW 2) Rafiqul Alam alias Rafiqul Islam contested the suit by filing written statement, who in his written statement as well as evidence admitted about the registration of the kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921. 

 30. Upon a scrutiny of the evidence on record, it appears that the Exhibit 1, kabulyat dated 7-11-1921 is admittedly a registered document of 1921, the defendants also claimed their title by virtue of the same kabuliyat (exhibit-1). No dispute was raised in the trial Court as to its registration nor nay finding on this point in the judgment of the Subordinate Judge, Barisal. The records shows that the trial Court called for the original kabuliyat from the Collectoriate. Therefore, we do not find any substance in the last branch of argument of Mr. Abdul Quayum that the kabuliyat (Exhibit 1) is an unregistered document particularly when the same is nobody's case. 

 32. Be that as it may, the records of rights of the Government which at best are evidence of possession at the time when such records are prepared and not an evidence of title. This is a well-established principle of law. A registered kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over the other records of rights, until and unless such kabala/kabuliyat is cancelled on a specific allegation of fraud by any civil court in an appropriate civil suit. 

 35. On an overall consideration of the facts, circumstances and the materials on record, we are of the opinion that the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court below suffers from illegalities in many folds, it cannot be sustained in law and is liable to be set-aside. 

 Let a copy of the judgment along with lower Court's record be sent down at once.

lawyer:
Md. Ashad Ullah, Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman Advocate-on Record ------ For the Petitioner

Respondent Nos. 11-24 ------ Not represented
parties:

Afsarunnessa Khatun Chowdhury and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the petitioner and the proforma-respondent Nos. 21- 24 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 05 of 2002 in the Court of Joint. District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka praying for a declaration that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 152 of 1957 by the Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka on 28.05.1960 was not binding upon them. They stated, inter alia, that the land of Title Suit No. 152 of 1957 was part of C.S. Plot No. 67 under C.S. Khatian No. 174 and the total area of C.S. Khatian No. 174 of Mouja Dhanmondi, former Keranigonj Police Station and at present Dhanmondi Police Station was 60.13 acres and the superior landlords were Nezabot Ali Kha, Abdul Hakim and others. The land of the C.S. Plot No. 67 was owned and possessed by one Gopeswar Paul, son of late Bhubaneswar Paul as tenant under the superior landlord and C.S. record-of-rights was finally published in the name of tenant Gopeswar Paul. C.S. Plot No. 67 comprised   an area of 38.48 acres. Said Gopeswar Paul while owning and possessing the said land died leaving behind two sons, namely Nilkanta Paul and Harekrishna Paul as his heirs. Subsequently, Harekrishna Paul died leaving behind only son Debraj Paul as his heir. Said Nilkanta Paul and Debraj Paul while possessing the said land, sold 4 bighas of specific chala land out of total 38.48 acres of land of C.S. Plot No. 67 to one Sreejukta Kiron Chandra Bandapadhaya, son of late Binod Chandra Bandapadhaya vide registered deed No. 1845 dated 14.07.1933 and delivered possession to him. Thereafter, Kiron Chandra Bandapadhaya sold his entire purchased 4 bighas land, equivalent to 1.33 acres with trees standing thereon to Md. Shahjahan Bhuiyan, son of late Moulvi Mohammad Abdul Wahab Bhuiyan, predecessor of the present petitioner and opposite party Nos. 21-24 vide registered sale deed No. 4623 dated 18.08.1948 and handed over possession to them and they are in possession of the said land jointly. The Government, for the construction of the residence of Government employees, acquired 16.75 acres of land including 1.33 acres of C.S. Plot No. 67 owned and possessed by Md. Shahjahan Bhuiyan vide Land Acquisition Case No. 06 of 1948-49 and compensation was prepared in his name for an amount of Tk. 3,976.11. But the Government did not take possession of the entire acquired land including the land owned and possessed by the predecessor of the petitioner as the said land was not needed for the purpose for which acquisition proceeding was started, and the said land is a small unspecified part of a bigger plot. The compensation was not withdrawn by the predecessor of the petitioner and the said amount was deposited in the Government Revenue Accounts. Since possession of 1.33 acres of land owned and possessed by the predecessor of the petitioner was not taken over by the Land Acquisition Department, the said land remained in the possession of the petitioner's predecessor Md. Shahjahan Bhuiyan who died on 18.02.1982. On the recommendation of the Ministry of Works and Housing, the then Prime Minister directed release of the unused acquired portion of land of the owners in possession on 18.03.1974, and also directed to take back the compensation money from those awardees who had taken compensation, and further directed to publish Gazette Notification immediately in that regard. But the said direction was not acted upon. Ultimately, in the year 1984 decisions were taken by the Government for implementation of the earlier decision. Mrs. Salma Bhuiyan, mother of the petitioner on 19.06.1989 filed an application to the Minister, Ministry of Land for releasing the said property form L.A. Case No. 06 of 1948-49 and he directed the Additional Deputy Commissioner (L.A.) Dhaka to submit report after inquiry. Accordingly, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (L.A.), Dhaka after inquiry submitted report on 26.06.1989 to the Ministry of Land. In the said report it was clearly stated that the petitioners were in possession of the said property by constructing structures. The petitioner's property not having been released, they filed Title Suit No. 133 of 2001 in the Court of the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the Government for declaration of their 16 annas right, title and interest in the said ; 1.33 acres of land and the said suit is pending for disposal. The opposite party Nos. 1-18 or their predecessor got their names recorded in respect of 50 decimals of land out of total 1.33 acres of the aforesaid land ; of C.S. Plot No. 67 at the field level in the recent Dhaka City Survey and they filed appeal under Rule 31 of the State Acquisition Tenancy Rules, 1955 framed under State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and from the said case record, the petitioner found photocopy of the certified copy of the judgment and decree dated 28.05.1960 passed in Title Suit No. 152 of 1957 of the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka and the petitioner came to know that the opposite party Nos. 1-18 or their predecessor, suppressing the facts of the earlier title deed, possession of the petitioner's predecessors as well as acquisition proceedings, obtained a decree in respect of unspecified 50 decimals of land out of total 38.48 acres of land. The petitioner does not claim any interest in the suit land of the Title Execution Case No. 32 of 1962 but claim different land by way of earlier title document because of the question of the identity of the suit land. The said judgment and decree has cast cloud upon the right, title, interest and possession of the suit land of the petitioner because of identity of the suit land and the decretal land. As the heirs of late Md. Shahjahan Bhuiyan, they filed Title Suit No. 05 of 2002 before the District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka against the opposite party Nos. 1-18 and prayed for declaration that the judgment and decree passed on 28.05.1960 in Title Suit No. 152 of 1957 of the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka is not binding upon the plaintiffs of the present suit. 

 10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and other connected papers on record. 

 12. In the impugned judgment the High Court Division observed that as per the admission of the plaintiff-petitioner the suit land of Title Suit No. 05 of 2002 was acquisitioned vide L.A. Case No. 06 of 1948-49 and that the plaintiff-petitioner is yet to be successful in releasing the said suit property from the list of acquisition and requisition and that his right to the suit land is yet to be established. It was further noted that there is no record of rights in respect of the suit land in the name of the plaintiff-petitioner and that there is no rent receipt to show that the plaintiff-petitioner is in physical possession in the suit land. The High Court Division concluded that the plaintiff-petitioner is yet to establish his right, title and possession in the suit land by way of releasing the suit land from the list of acquisition and requisition. So long the plaintiff-petitioner is unable to establish his title and possession in the suit-acquired land he cannot get any relief of temporary injunction
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

lawyer:
Md Abdul Haque, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Md Mokleshur Rahman, Deputy Attorney-General with Ms Nusrat Jahan, Assistant Attorney-General—For the Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Golam Ambia (Harun) ------ Petitioner
Vs
Bangladesh and others ------  Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that Satish Chandra Datta and Ramesh Chandra Datta were the CS recorded tenant of the land under CS Khatian No. 1072 in the year 1941. Petitioner's father Abdul Aziz took settlement of 0.2385 acre land of CS Plot No. 1075 as under Raiyat under Satish Chandra Datta and Ramesh Chandra Datta. The father of the petitioner was possessing the land by paying rents to the original tenants by rent receipts. In the year 1971 during the Liberation War the rent receipts along with other documents of Abdul Aziz were destroyed. After the independence of the country Satish Chandra Datta and Ramesh Chandra Datta secretly tried to sale the land to elsewhere. Having come to know about the sale, the petitioner's father expressed his desire to purchase the land but Satish Chandra Datta and Ramesh Chandra Datta refused to sale the land to the father of the petitioner. They directed the petitioner's father to leave the possession of the land but Abdul Aziz, the father of the petitioner notoriously refused the title of Satish Chandra Datta and Ramesh Chandra Datta. Thereafter, the father of the petitioner excavated a pond in the suit land and by operation of law the status of Abdul Aziz as tenant was upgraded under Government. Abdul Aziz showed his papers to the employees of settlement and survey for the purpose of preparation of SA record in the name of Abdul Aziz. While Abdul Aziz was possessing the land by excavating pond thereon and by doing pisciculture there in the 1st week of June 1974 he orally gifted the land to his son, the petitioner and delivered possesion of the pond in favour of the petitioner. In the year 1976 petitioner's father died and in the year 1995 the petitioner desired to fill up the pond by earth with a view to constructing a market and residential house by taking loan from the Bank. For that purpose he went to the Office of the Tahsilder in the month of March 1995 and came to know that the land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the Government under Khas Khatian No. 1. 

 5. Mr Md Abdul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that right, title and possession of the petitioner duly confirmed by the competent Civil Court and the petitioner is legally entitled to pay rent for his land by opening a separate khatian in his name and the respondents are legally bound to receive rent from the petitioner for his land. He further submits that Board of Land Administration, Bangladesh, Dhaka circulated Memo No. (Q) X-46 /83-BLA dated 5-1-1984 for regulating the maintenance of record of rights in connection with the judgment and decree of the Civil Courts. He finally submits that the respondents by their malafide activities violated the Article 42 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 8. It appears from Annexure-A1 to the writ petition that the learned Assistant Judge, Bhaluka, Mymensingh by his judgment dated 29-6-1996 passed in Other Class Suit No. 27 of 1996 declared the title of the petitioner and also declared that the petitioner is in possession of the suit land. It also appears from Annexure-B to the petition that by judgment and decree dated 1-12-1998 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Mymensingh dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the Assistant Judge, Bhaluka. Against the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court respondent No. 1 filed Civil Revision No. 669 of 2004 before this Hon'ble Court and the Rule was discharged on 29-7-2008. Against the judgment and order to the High Court Division no appeal was preferred before the Appellate Division. After discharging the Rule the petitioner filed application to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Sadar, Mymensingh for mutating the land in his name and to receive rent from the petitioner by opening a separate khatian. But respondents did not consider his application and remained silent. Then the petitioner moved to this Court. It appears from the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court as well as appellate Court and the circular issued by the Board of Land Administration dated 5-1-1984 (Annexure-G) that sections 143 and 144 of the Act are intended for the purpose of Maintenance of Record of Rights. After passing the decree since the respondent No. 1 was the party and suit was decided and the appellate Court affirmed the judgment of the trial Court it is binding upon the respondents and they are legally bound to mutate the name of the petitioner as per judgment passed by the Courts below. In spite of filling application for mutation and for accepting rent stating all facts respondent No. 2 remain silent and did not mutate the name of the petitioner as per judgment and decree passed by the trial Court as well as the appellate Court. We find substance in the Rule. The Rule has got merit, which is liable to be made absolute.

4. At the trial the petitioners examined one witness in support of their case. While cross-examining PW 1 it was suggested to him by the defence that one. Bhaduri Bibi, wife of Ishaque Miah, is a co-sharer to the case land and she is a necessary party, although her name was not recorded in the record of rights. Thereafter the petitioners filed an application for adding the said Bhaduri Bibi as an opposite party in the case and to amend the pleadings accordingly. 

 6. Mr. HN Nondy, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners, submitted that due to accidental mistake Bhaduri Bibi was not impleaded as a party in the case. Moreover, her name was not recorded in the record of rights. The learned Counsel further submitted that in the written objection the opposite-parties raised the question of defect of parties in a most casual manner without making any specific averments in that direction. He further submitted that the court has enough power under Order VI rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure to allow any party to alter or amend his pleadings at any stage of the proceedings when such amendment is found necessary for the purpose of determining the real question in controversy between the parties. He further submitted that in the instant case addition of Bhaduri Bibi as a party to the proceeding by way of amendment of the petition will not in any way prejudice the opposite parties by putting any impediment in their defence and, as such, the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in rejecting, the petitioners application for amendment of the pleadings by way of addition of a party to the case. He further submitted that Order J rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure also confers wide powers upon the court to strike or add parties at any stage of the proceedings when such striking out or addition is found necessary for effectually and completely adjudicating upon and settling all questions Involved in a suitcase.

2. Plaintiff-respondent No. 1 filed the aforesaid suit in the court of the Assistant Judge in the then Upazila Ramu against the appellant and others for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction and alternatively for recovery of possession in respect of 3.32 acres of land appertaining to RS Khatian No. 171, more fully described in the schedule to the plaint. Plaintiff's case, briefly, was that the entire disputed land belonged to two brothers, Jamaluddin and Alimuddin, in equal shares. Although the disputed land was recorded in the CS record pi rights in the name of Jamaluddin alone, Jamaluddin and Alimuddin lived in the same mess and Jamaluddin was the elder of the two brothers. While Jamaluddin and Alimuddin equally possessed the disputed land, Alimuddin died leaving son, Abdul Hamid and daughter, Salema Khatun, as his heirs. Abdul Hamid then kot mortgaged 2 kanis of land to one Badiuddin for a period of 5 years from 1281 to 1285 Mogi Era corresponding to 1919-1924 AD for securing a loan of Taka 38.00 by executing and registering a deed of mortgage on 16-6-1919. Jamaluddin then died leaving son, Abdul Majid and daughter, Saderannessa. Abdul Majid went away to Burma and died there unmarried leaving full sister Sadernncssa and father's brother's son, Abdul Hamid as his heirs. During the RS operation the shares of Saderannessa and Abdul Majid were wrongly recorded in the names of Badiuddin and his brother's son at his instance. In fact, Badiuddin used to possess 2 kanis of land as mortgagee of Abdul Hamid and taking advantage of this fact, Badiuddin got the RS record of rights recorded in his name and in the name of his relations. Abdul Hamid by inheritance as stated above acquired 12 annas share in the disputed land. While Abdul Hamid was in possession of his share he again kot mortgaged the same land to one Kalachand by executing and registering a deed of mortgage on 15-5-1933 and subsequently he redeemed the said mortgage in case No. 606/2 of 1940 before the Special Debt Settlement Board and obtained possession therein. Abdul Hamid then died leaving two sons, namely the plaintiff Haji Golam Bari and Kala Mia and two daughters, Kulsuma Khatun and Omda Khatun and s widow, Sonaban, as his heirs. The plaintiff purchased the shares of his co-sharers including the share of Salema Khatun by different registered kabalas Saderannessa died leaving son, Sahar Mulluk and husband Tamim Golam as her heirs. The defendants, some of whom are the heirs of the first mortgagee, Badiuddin threatened the plaintiff with dispossession. Hence the suit. 

 4. The learned Judge of the High Court Division observed in the impugned judgment that the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit by a somewhat perfunctory judgment without recording any finding as to the matters in dispute agitated by the parties before him. The learned Assistant Judge however found that Badiuddin and others had been in possession of 4 kanis of land corresponding to 1.60 acres as mortgagee of Abdul Hamid from time immemorial and, as such, after their death, the heirs of the mortgages, the contesting defendants and others had acquired good title therein. 

 5. On appeal by the plaintiff, the learned Subordinate Judge, Cox's Bazar found that the disputed land originally belonged to Jamaluddin and Alimuddin and Alimuddin's son, Abdul Hamid, acquired a total of 1.66 acres out of it by way of inheritance and he kot mortgaged 1.60 acres therefrom to Badiuddin and Nazu Mia. The High Court Division observed that the learned Subordinate Judge did not record any definite finding as to the share of Jamaluddin although he appeared to disbelieve the story of surrender of his share to Sarada Kripa Lala and settlement thereof with the defendants' predecessors. He, however, did not record any finding whether the plaintiff had acquired interest in the -/8/ annas share of Jamaluddin in the manner alleged in the plaint. The learned subordinate Judge found that Badiuddin and Nazu Mia and in their absence, their successive heirs acquired valid title to the mortgaged land i.e. 1.60 acres since the right of redemption had already been barred as neither Abdul Hamid nor his heirs came to seek redemption of the said land within a period of 60 years. The appeal was accordingly dismissed by judgment and decree dated 26-2-86. Then the aforesaid revision was filed by the plaintiff respondent in which, as already noticed, the impugned judgment and order were passed. 

 14. Mr. B Hossain, learned Advocate-on-record appearing for the plaintiff-respondent, has made a vain attempt to support that part of the impugned judgment to which exception, as noticed above, has, in our opinion, been rightly taken.

2. The short facts for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party government as plaintiff, instituted a suit for declaration against the petitioner as defendant for a declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Misc. Case No. 142 of 1970 by the learned Munsif, Sadar Mymensingh is fraudulent, illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff, alleging inter alia that the suit land measuring 0.200 Sahasrangsha recorded in Plot Nos. 7025 and 7026 under new Khatian No. (SA) No. 2383 and old Plot No. 702 under old Khatian No. 95 of Mouza Mymensingh town is Government Khas land; that the present petitioner filed Misc. Case No. 141 of 1970 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Sadar Mymensingh for correction of the record of rights in her name and obtained an ex parte decree therein on 9.1.71 beyond the knowledge of the opposite party-government; that thereafter AGP Mymensingh filed an application for setting aside the aforesaid decree under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure but the same was eventually dismissed for default on 28.2.72; that thereafter, the government filed Misc. Case No. 72 of 1972 and the same was dismissed on contest on 13.2.73; that on the basis of the aforesaid ex parte order the defendant (present petitioner) sought for the correction of the record of rights in her name before the CO (Rev), Sadar Mymensingh on 22.12.79 when the plaintiff came to know about the said ex parte order and hence the suit, being Suit No. 492 of 1981, for a declaration for cancellation of the ex parte order dated 9.1.71 passed in Misc. Case No. 142 of 1970. 

 3. The petitioner contested Suit No. 492 of 1981 by way of filing written statement denying all material allegations as contained in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation, that the landlord Moharaja Shashi Kanta Acharjya Bahadur of Mymensingh being 16 annas owner settled the suit land in favour of the petitioner in 1347 BS on proper Nazar Salami and since then she has been owning and possessing the same in her own right and adversely against all others on payment of rent with the appropriate authority; the suit land being wrongly recorded in the Collector's Khas Khatian she filed the said Misc. Case No. 142 of 1970 in the 1st Court of Munsif Mymensingh under section 143(a) of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act for correction of the ROR and the present plaintiff Government i.e. opposite party, contested the case by filing written objection; that on 09.01.71 when the Misc. Case was fixed for peremptory hearing, the opposite party government filed hazira but was found absent on repeated calls and the suit was taken up for hearing and after recording deposition of the petitioner and marking the relevant documents as exhibits the court was pleased to allow the said Misc. Case; that the opposite party Government had full knowledge of the said ex parte order dated 09.01.71; that the opposite party Government filed Misc. Case No. 23 of 1971 under Order 9 rule 13 CPC for setting aside the said ex parte order but the said Misc. Case No. 23 of 1971 was dismissed for default on 28.02.72 and thereafter the present plaintiff Government filed another Misc. Case No 72 of 1972 which was also dismissed on contest on 13.2.1973.

full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that opposite parties 1-5 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 121 of 1999 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Shreepur, Gazipur for declaration of title in the suit land measuring an area of 1.66 acres as described in the schedule to the pliant. In the plaint they stated that Tonai Sheikh, Fazar Ali Sheikh and Ayub Sheikh were the recorded tenants of the suit land. Tonal died leaving his 3 sons Hasen, Hossain and Abdul. Abdul sold out 0.70 acres through a kabala dated 08-1-1955 to plaintiffs 1-3 and handed over possession thereof. Mahar Ali died leaving his father and mother as heirs. Fazar Ali died leaving his only daughter Meherjan who sold her share to Soude Ali and Sujjad Ali. Nayeb Ali died leaving behind his son Nazar Ali who got 2.61 acres as heir and 0.1166 acres from his son Mohar Ali, i.e., in total 2.72 acres. He died leaving behind his wife Monisa Nessa daughter Helena and plaintiffs 1-4 with 6 sons. Ahmed Ali sold out 0.0525 acres on 09-4-1996 to plaintiff 5. Nazar Ali during his life time sold some land to Helena and Monisa on 16-9-1989 and further gifted 0.28 acres to Mirza Ali and Mojibor Rahman through a heba. Shamser Ali sold 0.07 acres through a kabala dated 4-1-1992 to Mojibor and the latter sold the same to plaintiff 3 on 4-10-1994 and handed over possession thereof. Mojibor further gifted 0.14 acres to plaintiffs 3 and 4 on 19-1-1991. Shamser Ali sold 0.105 acres on 5-3-1976 to plaintiff 1 and handed over possession. Helena sold 0.0975 acres on 22-11-1994 to plaintiff 4. SA khatian was correctly prepared in the name of Nazar Ali. The plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land measuring 1.66 acres. They went to pay rent to the tahshil office on 13-10-1999 but the tahshildar refused to accept it showing reason of preparing record in the name of government. The above record of rights clouded the title of the plaintiffs over the suit land. Hence the suit for declaration that RS record prepared in the name of government is erroneous. 

 3. Defendant 2 government contested the suit by filing written statement. They contended that the suit has been filed on false statements, it is bad for defect of parties and not maintainable in the present form. They further stated that CS record was prepared in the name of Tonai Sheikh and others and SA record was prepared in the name of Nayeb Ali and others in respect of khatians 451 and 456. The land of SA khatian 150 was recorded in RS plots 977, 987, 984. 986, 902, 911, 1999. 1022. 1012. 1017, 902 and 903 in the name of the government. The above recent record has been correctly prepared and, as such, the suit would be dismissed. 

 4. The trial Court framed 5 issues to adjudicate the matter in dispute. During trial the plaintiffs examined 4 witnesses and produced their documents as exhibits 1-4 while the defendants government examined 1 but produced no document in support of their claim. However the Assistant Judge, Shreepur, Gazipur by the judgment dated 28-11-2000 decreed the suit declaring plaintiffs' title in the suit land. The Court further declared that RS record prepared in the name of the government is erroneous. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendants preferred appeal before the District Judge, Gazipur bearing Number 85 of 2011 with an application for condonation of delay of 3700 days. Learned District Judge kept the appeal for admission hearing. Subsequently upon hearing he rejected the application for condonation of delay by the judgment and order passed on 16-6-2011 and refused to admit the appeal being barred by limitation. Being aggrieved by the defendant-appellants moved in this Court in a revisional application with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 3299 days upon which this Rule was issued. 

 5. Ms Rahima Khatun, learned Deputy Attorney-General takes me through the revisional application the application for condonation of delay and the supplementary affidavit filed on 03-6-2024. She then refers to the cases of Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Divisional Forest Office); Mymensingh Forest Division vs. Abdur Sobhan and others, 73 DLR (AD) 1; Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Rcingpur vs. Hasrat Mohani and others, 2 (ADC) 715; Khairullah (Md) vs. ADC (Revenue) and another; 54 DLR (AD) 13 and Divisional Forest Offices; Village 12, Mohakhali, Dhaka and another vs Md Abdul Hossen @ Amir Hossen and others, 66 DLR 661 and submits that although the delay in this case is inordinate but in the application for condonation of delay and in the supplementary affidavit sufficient reason for it has been shown. The government has to move through different organs for taking opinion in filing revision and for that reason' delay occurred. In the cited cases our apex Court expressed of taking lenient view in disposing an application filed by the government for condonation of delay. In this case if the facts and circumstances narrated in the application is considered the delay may be condoned to secure the ends of justice. She takes me through the judgment passed by the trial Court and submits that the suit in the present form was not maintainable and, as such, no decree can be passed in it. Admittedly, the suit land has been recorded in the name of the government as khas. In view of the ratio laid in the aforesaid cases, the delay may be condoned giving a chance to the petitioners to hear the appeal on merit. The Rule, therefore, would be made absolute. 

 7. I have considered the submissions of both the sides, the application for condonation of delay the supplementary affidavit, the counter affidavit, the other materials on record and the ratio of the cases cited by the parties. 

 8. It appears that the opposite parties to this Rule instituted the original suit praying for declaration of title and for further declaration that the RS record prepared in name of the government is erroneous. The petitioners government contested the suit by filing written statement and examined a witness on their behalf. However, the trial Court decreed the suit on contest by its judgment and decree passed on 28-11-2000. After long lapse of 3700 days of the period of limitation the defendant government filed an appeal before the District Judge, Gazipur with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act to condone the delay of 3,700 days. In the application for condonation of delay the appellants had assigned reason only that when the plaintiffs filed application for correction of the record of rights then they came to learn about the judgment and decree passed by the Assistant Judge and, as such, the delay occurred. The District Judge found the explanation offered by the petitioners not satisfactory, rejected the application for condonation of delay and consequently refused to admit the appeal being barred by limitation which has been challenged in the revisional application.
