full_judgment:
3. Short facts are that the predecessors of present respondent Nos.17-34 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.81 of 1994 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Munshigonj for partition of the suit property and declaration that the RS record is wrong in respect of the suit land contending inter-alia that the suit land belonged to ex-landlords Bouddanath Sharma and others, who took khas possession of the suit land from the CS tenant and as they defaulted in paying rent the Zaminder of the suit land by pattan settlement gave to Montazuddin (predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-7), Abdul Hamid (predecessor of plaintiffs) and Mohammad Bepari (predecessor of defendant Nos. 8-10) on 28th Poush of 1362 BS through Amalnama supported by Dakhila. But, in the Amalnama the shares of Montazuddin were wrongly written as 10 annas, 13 gondas, 1 kara, 1 kranti, while that of Abdul Hamid were 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 kranti. The original Amalnama was lost, but photocopy of that was with the plaintiffs. In spite of wrong insertion of shares in the name of Montazuddin, the three settlers possessed the suit land in equal shares and accordingly SA Khatian No.117 was rightly prepared in their names. Abdul Hamid died leaving behind his wife Amina Khatun, who inherited 1/3 share left by Abdul Hamid and she gifted that share equivalent to 0.861/2 acre by two Heba-bil-Ewaz deeds to plaintiff No.1, Md Panchu Dhali and plaintiff No.2 Saifunnessa. Since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by paying rent and mutated their names. The suit land was partitioned by metes and bounds. During RS preparation of record the names of plaintiffs were primarily recorded in the RS khatian Nos.233 and 380, but finally the names of the plaintiffs were omitted. The names of the defendants were recorded in the said RS Khatian omitting the names of the plaintiffs. On the basis of these wrong RS records, the defendants are claiming additional land in which they have no right. So, the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land became clouded. The plaintiffs requested the defendants in the first part of Ashar of 1401 BS for partition, which was denied by the defendants. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the suit. 

 5. Defendant Nos.1-7 contended, inter-alia, that their predecessor Montazuddin took the suit land by pattan/ settlement of 10 annas, 13 gondas, 1 kara, 1 kranti and he also took settlement of remaining 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 karas and 2 krantis in the Benami of Abdul Hamid. Practically Montazuddin was owner of 16 annas, i.e. 2.59 acres of land. Montazuddin paid rent by himself in the Zaminder's Seresta for the entire suit land and had been in possession of the entire suit land by erecting dwelling house and by cultivation. Abdul Hamid never possessed the suit land nor did he pay rent thereof. In the year 1961 Abdul Hamid requested Montazuddin to accord permission for Mohammad Bepari to live in some portion of the suit land and, therefore, Montazuddin permitted Mohammad Bepari to live in a small part of the suit land. In SA khatian, owner Montazuddin, his Benamder Abdul Hamid and licensee Mohammad Bepari's names were recorded. Montazuddin paid rents for the suit land and died leaving defendant Nos.1-7, who had been in possession of the suit land. Before preparation of RS record 10 decimals from plot No.60 and 17 decimals from plot No.63 were occupied by the Government for constructing road and only 1.44 acres of land was recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 1-6 in RS khatian No.223. In order to avoid litigation, the defendants admitted this RS record. The plaintiffs' deeds are forged. Abdul Hamid possessed only 2 annas and he had two wives. So, the plaintiffs cannot claim more than the share inherited by each wife. Defendant Nos.1- 7 possessed 1.44 acres of land. The plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 8-10 have no possession. So, the suit should be dismissed. 

 6. The defendant Nos. 8-10 contended, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to Zaminder Mohini Kumar Dey and Kangali Dey and they settled the suit land to Mohammad Bepari and put him in possession. At the time of SA record, SA khatian No.117 was correctly made in the name of Montazuddin Morol, Abdul Hamid and Mohammad Bepari. By amicable partition total 2.59 acres of land was possessed by them erecting dwelling houses in equal shares. Mohammad Bepari got 0.86 acre of land in his share. Mohammad Bepari's name was correctly recorded in the RS khatian No.580. Mohammad Bepari died leaving behind 3 sons (defendant Nos.8-10), one daughter Rana Akter and wife Morjina Begum, and the heirs have been possessing 0.82 acre of land by putting pillars and 0.04 acre in ejmali in the pond. The plaintiffs have no title and possession over the suit land. So, the plaintiffs' suit is not maintainable. Defendant Nos. 8-10 prayed for a separate saham of 0.86 acre of land. 

 8. Being aggrieved, defendant Nos.1-7 preferred Title Appeal No.83 of 1996 before the District Judge, Munshigonj challenging that the defendant Nos. 8-10 were not entitled to get any share and RS record No. 223 that was declared wrong is illegal. On transfer the appeal was heard by the Additional District Judge, Munshigonj, who by his judgment and decree dated 8-10-1998 dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Then defendant Nos.1-7 filed Civil Revision No.623 of 1999 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was made absolute in part by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court in Title Appeal No. 83 of 1996 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court. The judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court in Title Suit No. 81 of 1994 so far as it relates to giving 1/3 share of saham to the defendant Nos. 8-10 declaring the RS Khatian No. 223 wrong was also set-aside. 

 13. Mr Md Ruhul Amin Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appeared for respondent Nos.1, 3, 4, 6, 8 & 12-15, Mr Md Taufique Hossain, learned Advocate-on-Record appeared for respondent Nos. 17-21, Mr Md SR Khoshnabish, learned Advocate-on-Record appeared for respondent Nos.29-31 and Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Senior Advocate for respondent No. 36 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

 15. In this case predominant factor is the Amalnama or settlement dated 28 Poush 1362 B.S. which was exhibited by both the plaintiffs and the defendant Nos. 1-7, basing on which the High Court Division held that both the Courts below arrived at a decision on the basis of the Amalnama but failed to consider the names of the parties in the Amalnama which is misreading and non-consideration of the contents of the Amalnama because it clearly shows that the share of Montaz Uddin Morol is 10 annas 13 gonda 1 kara 1 karanti that is 2/3 share and Abdul Hamid Sarder 5 annas 6 gonda 2 kara 2 karanti that is 1/3 share. Furthermore, the Amalnama is an old document produced from proper custody which entitles that the document is genuine. SA and RS records are not document of title and the Amalnama, the document more than 30 years old, shall prevail over the record of rights and would remain in force unless same is cancelled by appropriate civil Court. 

 18. The trial court judged that the title and possession of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 8-10 are proved by dint of the oral and documentary evidence adduced therein. It was also proved that the SA khatian No. 117 was correctly recorded in the names of the predecessors of the contesting parties in equal shares. Moreover, possession of defendant Nos. 8-10 and that of the plaintiffs are also admitted by the defendant nos. 1-7. The defendant nos. 1-7 or their predecessor neither protested the separation of jama nor the mutation in the names of the defendant Nos.8-10 regarding the 1/3 portion of the suit land. 

 20. On the basis of documentary evidences it is proved that the defendant Nos. 1-7 could not establish the settlement to be genuinely a deed of title. And it is evident that the same is a rent receipt having incorporated the essential ingredients of a rent receipt. Moreover, the said rent receipt does not include the name of the predecessor of defendant Nos. 8-10. But, subsequently, during the operation of SA record of rights the defendant Nos. 8-10's predecessor got his name recorded in SA Khatian and strengthen his title in the suit land on par with the predecessors of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-7. The said SA Khatian not being challenged by the predecessors of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-7 had acted upon. 

 21. Moreso, the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-7 failed to prove that the suit land was recorded during the period of the SA operation on the basis of the alleged settlement/amalnama. Thus, after expiry of nearly about 80 years, we find no reason to believe the so-called settlement as the document of title. However, any amalnama, dakhila and registers of Zamindary period should be believed to be true when SA record would have been published in pursuant to those documents accordingly. 

 22. So, defendant Nos.8-10 being the successor of the SA recorded tenant Mohammad Bepari, are entitled to get separate saham of 86 decimal in the suit land. 

 "The other contention of the respondent that settlement taken by Taiyab Ali from Charubala as was not established, the plaintiff by purchase from Taiyab Ali in the year 1963 did not acquire any right, title and interest in the land in suit and consequently as the courts below were in error in decreeing the suit the High Court division committed no error in setting aside the said decree is also of no merit as the trial Court as well as the appellate court on consideration of the evidence both oral and documentary, have arrived at the concurrent finding that Taiyab Ali, vendor of the plaintiff took settlement of the land in suit from the admitted owner Charubala it may be mentioned High Court Division while setting aside the decree in the suit failed to advert itself to the materials upon placing reliance whereon the court of first instance and the appellate court arrived at the finding that Taiyab Ali, vendor of the plaintiff took settlement in 1357 BS of the land in suit and in his name SA record was prepared and the plaintiff purchased the land in the year 1963. The High Court division also failed to notice the fact that while settlement to Nurul Islam by charubala in the year 1359 BS was not established as genuine then the claim of the defendant No. 1 in respect of the land in suit by purchase from the person who said to have been taken settlement in 1359 BS did not vest any title in him."

 4. In the plaint, it has been started further that the schedule land had belonged to Ras Bihari Das alias Ramani Mohan Das who died intestate on 10th Cartik 1365 B.S. and he took possession of the property of schedule 1 and 2 after the death of said Rahmani Mohan and was growing paddy and was also enjoying the same. The said Rahmani Mohan Das during his life time created 2(two) debutter deeds dated 27th Chaitra 1333 B.S. 18' of Falgun 1351 B.S. respectively of the land described in the schedule of the plaint with intention to defraud his creditors. The said Ramoni Mohan had huge debts. The said deeds were created in the name of Sree Sree Mohan Prabhu and Sree Sree Sriman Gopal Jew Deties. In fact, the aforesaid deities had no existence at all and the aforesaid debuttar documents were never acted upon and that the suit properties were never treated as Debuttar properties during the life time of the donor Ramani Mohan Das. The creation of the alleged documents came to the knowledge of the plaintiff after his taking over possession of schedule 1 and 2 lands. The defendant no. 1 (since decased Brajangana Baishnabi) falsely asserted that the entire properties of Ramani Mohan Das was debuttar property and she was a Shebait. The suit land was recorded in the name of Ramani Mohan Das Baishnab as a secular property and he realized the Rent from the tenants by granting Largos (receipts) by filing rent suit in his own name. He also sold land to Asgar Ullah by registered deed dated 29 Maghs, 1358 B.S. in his personal capacity. The defendant No.1 Braja Bala Das meternal aunt of Ramanbi Mohan Das. She took her name as Brajangana Baishnabi and she was very cunning, while Ramani Mohan was simple and innocent person and used to live in the Akhra and taking advantage of Ramani's old age and simplicity and for deriving illegal gains managed to file 3 rent suits no. 42 43 and 44 of 1958 in the court of Munsif, 1st  Court, Sylhet in the name of the deities styling Ramani Mohan as Shebait, so that she being a Baishnabi might succeed him as next Shebait. The rents suit were filed to create evidence concerning the suit land that such land were debuttar Property. The said lady gave Ramani Mohan Das to understand that the property of the Baishnab will be taken by the Government and the only records for the same is to show the property as the debutter. After wholesale acquisition of rent receiving interest a sum of Ruppes 2001/86 paisa was assessed in the name of Ramani Mohan Das. The plaintiff after the death of Ramani Mohan filed objection and his name was recorded in place of Ramani in most of the IchatiAns including compensation assessment rolls. Said defendant No.1 Barja Bala Baishnabi filed title suit no. 301/1958 for permanent injunction for restraining the plaintiff from receiving compensation money from the government. In the said suit, the present plaintiff was restrained to get compensation until his title is declared in the properly instituted title suit. In the last week of May, 1969 the said Braja Bala in collusion with the avowed enemies of the plaintiff took step to dispossess him from the suit land, the plaintiff then constrained to file this suit. 

 resource and he had money leading business as well as he was pious. He had been leading a life like a Baishnab and then he actually adopted Baishnab and took the name Ramani Mohan Das Baishnabi and he had installed the deities namely Gopal Jew Moha Prabhu Akhra of Raikhal in his own homestead and his homestead had turned into Akhra Bari which was known as Gopal Jew Moha Prabhu Akhra of Rakhail. To make a permanent arrangement for the maintenance of the Akhra and perpetual Sheba — puja Ramani Mohan Das made a gift of the major portion of his properties to the said deities on 27th Chaitra, 1333 B.S. He divested his interest in the debuttar properties and remained a founder Shebait of the deities. He acquired some properties by the income of previous debater and on 151 of Falgoon 1351 B.S. he made another deed of gift of some more properties and in the deed mentioned the time of successions of Shebait ship of deities and also mentioned some other terms for proper management. He never revoked or cancelled those deeds either expressly or by implication. During the last settlement and survey operation the suit properties with some other properties through mistake were 'recorded in his name Raman Mohan Das Baishnab (Ramani Mohan Das Baishnabi) without mentioning his name of the Shebait of the deities. Knowing this said Ramani Mohan filed application for correction of record of rights and rivisional case no.32 of 56-57 of the office of the A.D.C. (Revenue) Sylhet was started and an order was passed for such correction as prayed for but due negligence of some of the officials of the office of A.D.0 (Revenue) the order was not carried out and previous record continued without rectification and taking advantage of this wrong recording, the plaintiff with the influence of proforma defendant nos. 2-13 filed the suit for illegal gain and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. Mr. Fazlul Haque the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant petitioners has taken us through the judgment of the courts below and evidence, both oral documentary as marked exhibits by the Trial Court and submitted that the learned Assistant Judge on proper discussions of the oral and documentary evidence decided the issue 'No.4 that the plaintiffs is not in possession of the suit property and that the deed- of gifts made in favour of the deities in the year 1333 and 1351 B.S. were acted upon, but the Appellate Court without properly adverted to the evidence has reserved those findings and that judgment being not a proper judgment of reversal has committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further contended that issue No.6 and 7 were decided against the plaintiffs and that the Appellate Court has not reversed the findings of the Trial Court to the effect that the plaintiff had failed to produce any witness to prove the name of any creditor of late Ramani Mohan before the Court nor any name of any creditor was mentioned in the plaint to prove that the deed of gift in faour of the deities were executed and registered by Ramani to defraud the creditor and arrived at an erroneous findings which has resulted an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The Appellate Court has utterly failed to consider that Rash Behari Das became a Baishnab and not only be changed his name as Ramani Das Baishnab but also changed his life style and in doing so he and dedicated his property in the name of the deities and his homestead was turned into Akhra Bari which are being transpired from exhibit "Go Series" and that the Appellate Court also failed to notice that some of the properties were recorded in the name of the deities and some of the lands of Raekhail Mouja were recorded in the name of Ramani for which Ramani filed an application before the A.D.0 (Revenue), Sylhet for correction of record of rights in the name of the deities, which has been marked as exhibit-Cha and his intention thereby, was proved that he dedicated his whole life for religious purpose but the teamed Appellate Court arrived at an erroneous decision in setting aside the judgment of the Trial Court which has clearly caused failure of justice. The Appellate Court on the face of the record has erred in recording his self contradictory and misconceived findings while considering the evidence of PW.2 regarding Akhra Bah and also made findings as to Braja Bala Baishnabi without considering the evidence to its true perspective but arrived at an erroneous findings and decision and thus acted upon erroneous view which has occasioned failure of justice. He further contended that the Appellate Court has grossly misread the evidence of PW.2 and DW.1 in as much as the deities are now in the custody of the Shebait DW.1 in his own house and the homestead of Ramoni which is the Akhrabari has vacant house. Sheba-Puja of the deities has been performing by the committed approved by the learned District Judge but such fact and evidence were not correctly appreciated and came to the wrong finding which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He submitted further that the Appellate Court has come to wrong findings that Ramoni Mohan Das Baishnab during his life time realized rents from the tenants and also filed rent suits in his own name and from the exhibit 9(ka), 10-10(ka), it disclosed Ramoni himself did not implement the deed of gift in favour of deities are misconceived findings and those were not in issue before the court and recording finding beyond the scope of the suit has committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 11. The learned Advocate for the petitioner today has filed a supplementary affidavit and has taken ground No.10, 11, 12 and 13 in continuation of his grounds taken earlier in substantive Revisional Application and supporting the grounds very candidly submits that the Appellate Court has not at all reversed the finding of the Trial Court as to bringing of any witness to support basic contention of the plaintiff as to the creditors and also failed to appreciate the exhibit Ga(1) the application for correcting the S.A. Khatian contending that the schedule as stated in the application was not annexed with the application though the Trial court has recorded specific findings on those issues but the Appellate court has totally failed to reverse those findings and thus committed fundamental error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 12. The learned Advocate further contended that the trial Court has specifically recorded findings that the document of sale as stated in the plaint was not in the exhibit list and another document which has been produced before Trial Court and marked as exhibit-7 is not related to the debuttar property but such finding has not been reversed by the Appellate Court and Thus has committed error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate has also taken us through exhibit-"Uma", the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.59 of 1972 by the learned District Judge and also placed exhibit-"Cha" the certified copy of the order passed in Civil Revision No.1325 of 1973 and submitted that those exhibits clearly show that the committee had held a meeting and the President and Secretary of the Committee were nominated to act and managed the affairs of deities by people of the localities and the learned District Judge upon considering the real position of the deities and also evidence had approved the committee and the said order had not been reversed by the High Court Division but the Appellate Court recorded no findings, what so ever, as to those exhibits and has committed error of law and prays for making the rule absolute. 

 13. On the other hand Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the Senior counsel along with Mr. Serajur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing before this court in countering the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner has strait way submitted that the basic question raised before this court as to whether 2 registered Debuttemama were acted upon during the life time of Ramoni Mohan Das Baishnabi and whether, the plaintiff is only serving heir of the said Ramoni Mohan Das and contended further that nature of the deeds also have to be cor_6idered before considering the oral evidence. He submits that the Appellate Court has clearly found that the deeds though executed by Ramoni Mohan were never been acted upon and held on consideration of the evidence both oral and documentary and the plaintiffs is the only surviving heir of late Ramoni Mohan, the Appellate Court since settled the facts being a final court of facts, these warrant no interference by the Hon'ble court and thereby, the Appellate Court committed no error of law in reversing findings of the Trial court. He further contends that on the face of the deeds, it is to be further decided and held, whether the two documents are "Illusory" endowments and also to be considered the evidence in that angle and in order to arrive at such conclusion the court has to consider the behavior of dedicator and the evidence in as much as Ramoni Mohan during his life time got recorded his name in S.A. Khatian (exhibit-2, 2(ka), 2(kha) and 2(Chaa) and sold land vide exhibit No.7 treating the properties as personal and secular properties and to ascertain such facts, the documentary evidence were not properly considered by the Trial Court but the Appellate Court has considered those aspect on the basis of the evidence both oral and documentary of the case and legally reversed the findings of the Trial court and committed no error of law. Referring to exhibit-14, it has been submitted that in a suit for realization of arrear rent filed Rent Suit No.44 of 1958 by Sree Mati Braja Bala Baishnabi and another, and the Munsif Court, Sylhet came to the findings :- "The plaintiff' have exhibited a debattaranama Ext.-I, the perusal of which shows that this property along with other properties, was gifted to deity but Exts. A-B a decree and copy of plaint in R.S. 182/52, show that donor Ramoni Mohan dealt with this property as his private property long, long after the execution of debatturnama. Thus it is clear that subsequent conduct of donor shows that debatturnama was not acted upon. So 1 am convinced that plaintiffs have no locustandi to bring this suit on the basis of debatturnama which was not acted upon." Against the said judgment the plaintiff Shebait Braja Bala took appeal before the District Judge, Sylhet being No.16 of 1959 (Ext.15). The appeal was heard by the Second Additional Court of Subordinate Judge, who affirmed the judgment of the Trial Court holding "The learned Trail Court accepted the defendant's contention as of substance and held that the Debuttarnarna Ext.-1 was not acted upon. 1 also find nothing to differ from him. Exhibits A and B conclusively proves the defendant's contention that Ramoni Mohan even after executing Debuttarnama in the year 1351 B.S. in respect of the jama and holding in brought Rent Suit No.182 of 1952 in respect of same jama and holding in his individual capacity giving an absolute go-bye to Ext.]. This shows clearly that this Ext.1 was not acted upon nor was it meant to be acted upon by Ramoni Mohan even during his life time "This contention- of the tenant, defdts was corroborated to the fullest extent by plff. No.2. But 1 may observe here that there is an apparent clash of interest between plff. No.1 and plff. No.2 and for that purpose I would like to leave the question of title of plff. No.1 and 2 interest open for a decision in a properly constituted suit between them as there is no scope for any finding of their title in the present suit or appeal." Referring to exhibit-7, the learned counsel submitted that the Trial Court committed error of law in finding contrary to the recital of the deed in as much as the Trial Court without considering the original deed has drawn conclusion on surmises but in fact Ramoni Mohan executed deed on 11.2.1952 and the schedule of both the deeds indicated that the preliminary number remains the same and in view of such facts the Appellate Court upon discharging the entire evidence held that the deeds were not acted upon and thus committed no error of law. He further contends that from exhibit-"Uma" it would be evident that the last alleged Shebait had come to Sylhet but did not convene meeting but the Hindu locals allegedly held the meeting on 23.5.1972 and in the meeting the alleged committee for the management of the property was formed and for the self same property the plaintiff filed suit before 1972 and the plaintiff was not notified while convened the meeting by the locals which is also evident from the exhibit "Uma" and alleged committee admittedly had formed in the absence of the plaintiff and this vital aspect of the case has not been considered by the Trial Court. The learned Counsel further submitted that from the evidence of the DWs it has been indicated that "idol" / deities had been shifted to house of the Secretary, the alleged Shebait and the Shebait is residing in his personal property and thus public has got no excess there. It would be evident further from the evidence that the alleged deitie's house of Akhara Bari has got no existence, what so ever, in spite of such evidence on record, such basic point, the Trial Court has not at all considered but this vital aspect of the case has been thoroughly considered by the Appellate Court and held that the deities have no existence and consequently, held that the deeds were not acted upon and therefore, committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned counsel further submitted that the plaintiff is not bound by any action of the alleged committee to have taken after the filing of the suit in 1969 and such actions are bad in law and suffers from principle of Lis pendens, as completed under section 52 of the Transfer Property Act and the alleged recording of name of the alleged Shebait after 1969 has got no validity and as such, the plaintiff is not bound by such recording allegedly made in the name of the alleged deities, but such aspect of the case was not considered by the Trial Court. He submitted further that natural corollary is that admittedly the plaintiff is the only heir of Ramoni Mohan and after the death of Ramoni automatically, the title and the possession of the property had vested on the plaintiff, if no contrary title is established by producing any legal evidence and accordingly, the name of the plaintiff was recorded in the S.A. Khatian and paid the rents denying the existence of the deities, 

 2. Illusory endowment- Meaning of In the eye of law illusory endowment is no endowment, because its purpose is either deceptive or vague. It is void in consequence of uncertainly of purpose. It may also be void if it be violative of law or any public policy. A trust is not properly created in an illusory endowment. Where there is no real dedication of property but an attempt has been made to create a perpetuity in favour of donor's descendants, the gift to the deity is illusory. An illusory endowment is a sham endowment. In such endowment the donor does not divest himself of his rights in the property. Often the intention behind the creation of the endowment is to defraud the creditors or to evade other legal obligations. Whether an endowment is illusory or real can be ascertained from the true intention of the donor. 

 16. On perusal of the judgment of the Appellate Court, it transpires that the Appellate Court has reversed the findings and decision of the Trial Court and held that the dedication to have made by 2 documents by Ramoni Mohan had not been acted upon as the donor had not completely divested himself of all beneficial interest in the property given in endowment and that the plaintiff is the legal heir of the said Ramoni Mohan and he has interest in the land and further held perusing the exhibits, in as much as the judgments of the litigations have expressly disclosed that Ramoni Mohan Das during his life time realized rent from the tenants and also for arrear of rents had filed rent suits and his name also was recorded in S.A. Khatian which is evident from exhibit-Gha(1) and further that such recording of rights has not been challenged 

 18. The Appellate Court has held relying upon mainly on the S.A. Khatian exhibit 2-2('), sale deed dated 22/02/1952 exhibit 7 and order dated 5.1.1959 in rent suit no.44 of 1958 and also on the basis of the order passed in Rent appeal No.16 of 1959 (arose out of rent suit no.44 of 1958) that the plaintiff has been able to prove that during the life time of said Ramoni Mohan, he did not divest himself from the properties rather he mutated his name and realized rent. The A"ppellate Court also held that the plaintiff is admittedly the grand son of Ramoni Mohan and the title and possession naturally had vested in him. He also found that the deities were not kept in the Debuttar properties but allegedly preserved in the custody of the Secretary of the committee in his personal house and also found that alleged application made by Ramoni Mohan contained no schedule of the property and as such, recording of names in S.A. Khatian remained unchallenged and I am of the view that the Appellate Court has decided the matter to its true perspective considering the evidence both oral and documentary and law and in reversing the findings, it appears further that the Appellate Court has committed no error of law. I have also concentrated myself as to whether the deeds ' were acted upon and upon scrutiny found that the original maker of the deeds i.e. Ramoni Mohan had recorded his name in S.A. Khatian during his life time and Braja Bala tried to establish herself as the Shebait by filing rent suit but the Munsif, 1st Court, Sylhet in rent suit no.44 of 1958 which had clearly held that the deeds were not acted upon and such findings were affirmed by the Appellate Court with the opinion that in an appropriate constituted suit the fate of the deeds will be decided and accordingly, the plaintiff had filed the suit in 1969. It appears from the resolution of the meeting held on 23.5.1972 Braja Bala was not present. The life of the committee appears to have given by the learned District Judge till appointment of the Shebait and since the plaintiff has been able to prove that the dedication of properties made by Ramoni Mohan by 2 deeds were not acted upon and further held that the function of the committee thereby ceased and in holding as such, the Appellate Court has committed no error of law. It is in evidence that the del'ies are not being maintained in the land of the Debuttar property but kept in a private house of the Secretary and as such, the very purpose of dedication as it appears to have lost and as such, I am of the opinion that the plaintiff has been able to prove that the Endowments had been made were "Illusory endowments and "Illusory endowments" are sham endowments. In such endowment the donor does not completely divest himself of all beneficial interest in the property given in endowment. 

 19. It has been found from the evidence on record that the Secretary of the Committee had removed the temple in which those were installed and installed those in his private house, where the member of the Hindu community appears to have no excess and thus, the worshippers are depriving in giving Sheba-puja. 

 24. The office is directed to send down the lower courts records immediately.

full_judgment:
3. The defendants contested the suits by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the defendants were never the monthly tenants of the plaintiffs or of Baidyanath; that no landlord and tenant relationship existed between them and Srish Chandra Battacharjee was not a benamdar of Baidyanath Srish Chandra Bhattacharjee died leaving two sons Dhirendra Bhattacharjee and Birendra Bhattacharjee, Baidyanath Chatterjee was the karmachary (employee) of Dhiren Bhattacharjee and Biren Bhattacharjee who migrated to India immediately after partition of India. Dhiren and Biren Bhattacharjee settled the suit properties along with other lands of the suit plot to defendants' predecessor in interest, Khondaker Abdus Salam on 17-5-1950 at a rental of Taka 30 on receipt of a salami of Taka 4001 by executing an amalnama (amaldari) and that the defendants have been possessing the suit holding since then on the basis of the aforesaid settlement. Their further case is that Dhiren and Biren Bhattacharjee agreed to complete the transaction by executing registered documents in favour of the defendants predecessor in interest but they did not do so. They also asserted that the solenama filed in Title Suit No. 102 of 1958 was fraudulent and the plaintiffs did not acqire any interest in the suit property by virtue of the kabala dated 4-11-1961. 

 10. The case of the respondents, on the other hand, is that Srish Bhattacharjee was not a benamder of Baidyanath and he purchased the suit properties with his own money for his own benefit. On the death of Srish Bhattacharjee that property devolved upon his two sons, Dhiren Bhattacharjee and Biren Bhattacharjee who settled the same by executing an unregistered amalnama (amaldari) in favour of defendants' predecessor in interest on receipt of a salami of Taka 4001 and a rental of Taka 30 on 17-5-1950. Since then they are in possession and they were never tenants under Baidyanath or the plaintiffs. 

 12. The learned Counsel then argued that since the defendants or their predecessor were/was not parties in Title Suit No. 102 of 1958 brought by Baidyanath against Dhiren and Biren, sons of Srish Bhattacharjee, they are not bound by the sole decree passed in Suit No. 102 of 1958. It is true that the defendants or their predecessor were not parties in the suit. In our view, they were not necessary parties in the suit and, as such, they were not rightly made parties in the suit. He next submits that Exhibits 7, 8(a), 9 and 12(b) were not properly considered by the High Court Division and upon misconstruction of those documents the High Court Division wrongly held that the defendants are tenants under the plaintiffs and their 'predecessor in interest Baidyanath. Exhibit 7 is the copy of the order dated 31-5-1950 passed by the House Rent Controller on a petition filed by the defendants predecessors, Khandaker Ansar Ahmed praying for fixation of rent of house No. 12. The House Rent Controller fixed the rent at Taka 15. Exhibit. 8(a) is the copy of an order dated 9-1-1963 passed by the Assistant Settlement Officer, Khulna in Objection Case No. 808 under section 19(1) filed by the defendant Khandakar Ansar Ahmed against the preparation of record of rights. It shows that record of rights was not prepared in the name of defendants' predecessor but order was passed to record his possession in Col. 13 of the Khatian Exhibit. 9 is the copy of reply to the show cause filed by the second party Abdus Salam in a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before Mr SA Hamid, Magistrate 1st Class, Khulna on 21-3-1958. In this petition he clearly stated that he came to the then East Pakistan in 1950 as a refugee and has been residing in holding Nos. 12 and 13 of Ward No.4 of Khulna Municipality (now City Corporation) as monthly tenant. Exhibit 12(b) is the copy of deposition of Khandakar Ansar Ahmed, in the above noted proceeding under section 145,Code of Criminal Procedure as second party. In his deposition he categorically stated "In 1950 we migrated to Pakistan and occupied the disputed house in holding No. 12 of Ward No. IV. We also occupied holding No. 13. Dhirendra Bhattacharjee is the owner of both the holdings. He lived in Calcutta. We are tenants of holding No. 12 and paid rent. Exhibit. A series are rent receipts granted by Bidhu Bhusan who was the karmachari of Dhiren, Exhibit. B is the certified copy of the suit register of the House Rent Control Case for the disputed house." In his evidence he also stated "We occupied the house after settling rent Taka 15 was fixed as rent for holding No. 12 from House Rent Controller in 1950. I have no paper to show the fixation of rent. Previous to the rent control case, we used to pay Taka 18 per month as house rent for holding No. 12 I have rent receipt for holding No. 13 which I will not file." In his evidence he further stated that he would deposit the rent of the suit premises before the House Rent Controller after disposal of the pending case. 

 17. Admittedly the suit property was Non-Agricultural Property from before 1947 and the same is situated within Khulna Municipal Corporation. The defendants once claimed that they were monthly tenants under Srish Bhattacharjee and thereafter under his sons, Dhirendra and Birendra. They again claimed that they took settlement of the suit property by unregistered Amaldari from Dhirendra and Birendra on 17-5-1950. It is the settled principle of law that settlement of Non-Agricultural land within Municipality cannot be effected by unregistered document. The same must be effected by bilateral registered document executed by both the lessor and the lessee. Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 came into force on 28th October, 1949 and according to defendants' case they took settlement by unregistered amaldari on 17-5-1950 and, as such, the same is hit by section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act.

3. Further case of the plaintiffs is that they being illiterate simple village folk they entrusted Morals and employees of the Zamindars with recording of their names during the settlement operation and they believed that their names were correctly recorded in the settlement papers. Principal defendants disclosed on 1st/2nd Chaitra, 1381 BS that they purchased the suit land from the proforma defendants and asked the plaintiffs to make over possession of the same to them. Plaintiffs doubted their claim and enquired into the Tahsil Office and came to learn that the employees of the landlords in collusion with the settlement staff got the suit land recorded as Khas Dakhuli land of the landlords. Proforma defendants never claimed the suit land on the basis of the wrong records nor did the same affect their title. Principal defendants obtained void, fraudulent, collusive sale deed from some of the greedy proforma defendants after coming to learn about the recording of the suit land in their names and thus clouded the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The plaintiffs on the basis of their settlement and adverse possession beyond the statutory period of limitation to the knowledge of all acquired title in the suit land and, as such, they are entitled to get their title declared. 

 5. Contesting defendant Nos. 1 to 8, 10 and 13 denied the material allegations made in the plaint. They further averred that the plaintiffs suit is not maintainable and barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Their specific case is that Syedunnessa Chowdhurani, Khan Bahadur Gousuddin Ahmed Chowdhury and others did never settle the suit land 40 years ago or at any time with the plaintiffs at an annual rental of half a maund of paddy per kedar or any rent nor they realised any rent from them. Suit land was Khas dakhali land of the said landlords and the same was fallow land even during the land settlement operation and recorded as such in the name of the proforma defendants in the khatians. In 1380 BS principal defendants entered into an agreement with the proforma defendants to purchase the suit land at the rate of Tk. 1250.00 per acre and with the permission of the said owners principal defendant Nos. 14 to 19 sold 24 acre of the suit land in their 14 annas 12 gondas 35 tils share at a consideration of Tk. 30,000 to the principal defendants by a registered sale deed dated 22nd Falgoon, 1381 BS (27.3.75) and the said sellers relinquished all their right, title and interest in the said land in favour of defendants 1 to 13 and the principal defendants have been possessing the same along with 1 anna 7 gondas 3 koras 5 tils shares of proforma defendants 20 and 21 who could not execute and register the sale deed for some difficulties but made over possession of the same to the defendants 1 to 13. Plaintiffs failed to purchase the suit land as the principal defendants offered more money than they had offered and they filed the suit on false allegation of settlement. They had never any title and possession in the suit land. 

 8. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder along with Mr. Hemayet Hossain and Mr. Jotirmoya Deb. learned Advocates, appearing on behalf of Mr. Jitendra Narayan Deb for the appellants, placed before us plaint, written statement, deposition of the witnesses, impugned judgment and other materials on record. The learned Advocate submitted that the plaintiffs failed to establish their alleged claim of settlement of the suit land on the basis of Toka farags Ext. 1 series which are neither in the name of any of the plaintiffs nor any particulars of the suit land mentioned therein. He further submitted that the plaintiffs also failed to establish their alleged adverse possession beyond the statutory period of limitation. He further submitted that the suit land was recorded in the name of predecessor-in-interest of the proforma defendants in finally published Khatians after factual field survey in the locality and the suit land has been recorded as fallow land (layek-patiti/ Layek ura). 

 10. In this case admittedly the suit land belonged to the predecessors-in-interest of the proforma defendants and it was their vacant Khas land and finally published khatians Ext. A series recorded the same in the name of the said landlords as their Khas land. The question in whether the said landlords settled the same with the plaintiffs and or the plaintiffs acquired title therein by adverse possession. 

 13. There is no case of the plaintiffs that they entered into the suit lands forcibly at any point of time to the knowledge of the said landlords, who admittedly reside far away and who has no tahsil office in the locality, denying title of the said landlords. Admittedly suit land was recorded in the name of the landlords Sayedunnessa Chowdhurani and Khan Bahadur Gousuddin Ahmed Chowdhury and others in Khatian Nos. 16 and 112 of mouza Purnakhola and Khatian No. 581 of Mouza Chaluia Exts. A-(2) and the said land has been recorded as fallow land in khas possessions of the said persons. It is admitted by the learned Advocates of both the parties that at the time of acquisition of rent receiving interest under the SAT Act field survey operation for preparation of record of rights under the provisions of Sylhet Tenancy Act 1936 in the suit locality was going on and ultimately the record of rights were prepared and finally published under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as there was no previous settlement operation in the District of Sylhet. Relying on the evidence of PW 1 the learned Advocate for the respondents contended that the said Khatians were wrongly prepared in the name of the landlords. PW 1 in his deposition stated that during last settlement operation they entrusted Morals and Karmacharies of landlords to record the suit land in their name. But in cross-examination he admitted that he has other lands besides the suit land and those were correctly recorded in his name. We have already seen that there was no tahsil office of the Zamindars in the locality and as such entrusting Karmacharies of the Zamindars cannot be relied on. None has corroborated the PW 1 in this respect and he also failed to name the Moral or Karmachari whom the plaintiffs had entrusted for the purpose. Moreover, the plaintiffs never took care to enquire about the Khatians within the period of 12 years from the date of final publication of the Khatians in 1963 and they only enquired about the Khatians in 1975 when they came to know from the principal defendants about the sale of the suit land by the proforma defendants to the principal defendants. The plaintiffs neither claimed to have paid any rent to the Government from 1363 BS till the time of filing the suit in 1382 BS nor produced and proved any rent receipts. In view of the above it is difficult to hold that the said Khatians were not correctly prepared in the name of said Zamindars. Such finally published SA Khatians prepared after field survey operation stand on much better footing and more reliable than the SA Khatians made by merely revising the CS Khatians. 

 15. From the above discussion, it is clear that the plaintiffs' failed to prove their possession in the suit land Plaintiffs claim that they made the suit land fit for cultivation 40 years ago after taking settlement and grew paddy therein is also belied by the entry in the khatians Ext. A series classifying the suit lands as Layak patit layck/ura i.e. follow land in Khas possession of the predecessor of the proforma defendants. It is well settled that possession follows title. Even occasional surreptitious acts of possession on the part of the plaintiffs behind the back of such recorded owners who were admittedly residents of a distant place in the absence of any evidence of forcible entry in the land in denial of title of such owners cannot amount to adverse possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. 

 16. Court below did not assign any reason for finding the khatians Ext. A series to be erroneous and kabala Ext. C to have no legal effect, admittedly Syedunnessa Chowdhurani and others were the owners of the suit land and proforma defendants 14 to 21 as their heirs inherited the same. As the plaintiffs failed to establish their settlement of the same from the said landlords we find no reason how the court below could hold the said khatians in the names of the said landlords to be erroneous and the kabala in favour of the principal defendants to have no legal effect. Had the plaintiffs acquired any title in the suit land they would have paid rent for the same to the Government from 1363 BS after the acquisition of rent receiving interest. They utterly failed to make out any such case of payment of rent to the Government. How could the plaintiffs enjoy the suit land from 1363 BS till the time of filing the suit as claimed by them without paying rent to the Government? Any lay cultivator is quite conscious that he cannot enjoy the land without paying rent to the Government. Had the plaintiffs acquired any interest or title in the suit land they would have endeavored to pay rent to the Government and would have taken steps at the earliest opportunity to get the Khatians corrected in their names. But they have been sitting idle and now have arisen from their deep slumber after lapse of such a long time when the principal defendants purchased the suit land from the proforma defendants. On the other hand, we find from Ext. B series that the contesting defendants paid rents for the years 1379-82 BS vide Ext. B series. These go to show that all previous rents were paid by the recorded owners of the said land as stated by the DW 1 in cross-examination.

full_judgment:
The case of the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 168 of 1984, in short, was that the lands described in schedule 1 and 2 are the accreted lands of Nuruli Ganga river adjacent to C.S. Plot No.153 owned by Jibunnessa Khatun and others, after accretion while the suit land became fit for cultivation the predecessor of the plaintiff Alauddin Bepari took settlement of the same from its owner 40 years back by giving salami and paying taxes. The suit land was duly recorded in the name of Alauddin Bepari in Plot Nos. 101 and 153. Alauddin Bepari died leaving plaintiff as his heir. The defendants raised objection against the S.A. record of the suit land under section 30 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but became unsuccessful. The defendants reside near the schedule 2 property and in the first part of Agrahayan 1385 B.S. they forcefully dispossessed the plaintiffs from the schedule 2 property and hence the suit. 

 The case of the defendants is that the suit land is the accreted land and it is contiguous to Plot Nos. 154, 161 and 162. While the land started accreting gradually Jashimuddin took settlement of 101/2 pakhi of land from the original owner Jibunnessa Khatun by executing a kabuliyat which was registered on 14th Chaitra 1353 B.S. Subsequently Jasimuddin took settlement of 15 pakhi of land more from Jibunnnessa by two patta. Since taking settlement of those lands Jashimuddin possessed the same on payment of rent to the landlord and subsequently to the Government. He constructed his house on a portion of the suit land and possessed the rest through cultivation, all within the knowledge of everyone, including the plaintiffs. During S.A. operation the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of plaintiffs. The plaintiffs took advantage of the survey staff residing in their house and collusively managed to have the suit land recorded in their names in the S.A. khatian. The defendants had been residing on the suit land for about 30 to 35 years. 

 During pendency of Title Suit No.168 of 1984 Jasimuddin himself also filed Title Suit No.53 of 1987 in the same Court for declaration of title in the same land and also for correction of record of rights. Both the Title Suit No.168 of 1984 and Title Suit No.53 of 1987 were tried analogously. The trial Court, decreed Title Suit No.168 of 1984 and dismissed Title Suit No.53 of 1987 by the judgment and decree dated 29.06.1989. 

 The pith and substance of the submissions pressed to service by the learned Senior Advocate Mr. Farid Ahmed for the appellants is that the High Court Division while making the Rule absolute in both the revisions on setting aside the concurrent findings of both the Courts below gave a finding that both the Courts without discussing the evidence on record decreed Title Suit No.168 of 1984 and dismissed Title Suit No.53 of 1987. This findings of the High Court Division is perverse as because the trial Court as well as the appellate Court on relying on the S.A. and R.S. record of rights, farogs, rent receipts and the oral evidence regarding possession and subsequent dispossession of plaintiff of Title Suit No.168 of 1984 decreed that suit and dismissed Title Suit No. 53 of 1987. 

 In elaborating his submissions the learned counsel contends that the High Court Division while making the Rule absolute and setting aside the concurrent judgments and decrees of the Courts below, failed to point out the misreading, non-reading or non-consideration of any evidence on record and without reversing the concurrent findings of trial Court and appellate Court made the Rule absolute. 

 “The learned Advocate-on-record failed to point out that the consideration of evidence made by the High Court Division in the background of non-consideration and misreading of the evidence by the appellate Court was erroneous in any respect and the said Division was in error in arriving at the finding as to title and possession of plaintiff and thereupon in setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court. In that state of the matter we do not find any substance in the petition.” 

 “The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division having independently assessed the evidence and having found a case of non-consideration of material evidence on record and consequent non-reversal of material findings interfered with the finding of fact. To our mind, the revisional court is competent to interfere in a case of non-consideration of material evidence which is specifically material for the determination of the material issue, namely, the issue of shifting of the school to the new mouza.”

caseno: Civil Revision No. 109 of 1989 with Civil Revision No. 9963 of 1991.
lawyer:
Rafi Ahmed, Advocate-------For the Petitioner.
