Sadaran Bima Corporation-------Petitioner
VS
Sylhet Pauroshava and others-------Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff-appellant, in brief is that the suit land originally belonged to Sylhet Pourashava which was acquired by it in LA case No.109/1901-1902. The Sylhet Pourshava Board was superseded by Government of Assam by Notification dated 10-2-39 for two years and the properties of Sylhet Municipal board were vested to the Crown and during this period of supersession the Governor of Assam granted lease of the suit land for 30 years to Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. by a registered Lease deed dated 18-9-1939. The Sylhet Industrial Bank constructed a two-storied building on the suit Land and carried their business. The said bank faced with financial difficulties and later by the order of Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Ford William in Bengal dated 25-6-47 it was amalgamated with M/s Mohaiakshmi Bank Ltd. M/s Mohaiakshmi bank Ltd. which held the assets of Sylhet Industrial Bank Ltd. and transferred the suit land along with building and other structures thereon to Arjya Insurance Co. by a registered Kabala deed dated 23-2-48. During Last S/S operation of 1956-57, the suit land was recorded in the name of Arjya Insurance Co. The suit land along with building and other structures were requisitioned in LA Case No. 42/B of 1950-51. Subsequently the suit land along with building and other structures were treated as enemy/vested property in VP Case No. 58/68-69. Plaintiff-appellant by its memo No.514 dated 22-3-1978 prayed to Deputy Commissioner Sylhet for release of the suit property in favour of Pourashava and Deputy Commissioner Sylhet by his memo No. DV/LG/3PS-12/(1)/78/909 dated 20-7-1978 directed the plaintiff-appellant to take steps for correction of record of right in the name of Sylhet Pourashava. Accordingly application was made for correction of record of right whereon, after due notices, orders were passed on 28-8-1978 for correcting the record of rights of the schedule land in the name of the plaintiff-appellant. But the property was not being released, so Pourashava moved the matter to Ministry of LA and LR whereupon the Ministry called for a report from Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet but no report has yet been submitted. Plaintiff-appellant Pourashava also, took up the matter for release of the property with Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) who in his reply to the Pourashava stated that record of rights were corrected in the name of the plaintiff-appellant and that the suit land being enemy/vested property by NP Case No. 58/68-69 and under requisition in the Requisition Case No. 42/B/50-51 and thus, he requested for necessary action in such content. On the other hand, the defendant respondent No. 1 Sadaran Birr a Corporation moved to the Ministry of Commerce and Ministry which advised the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Sylhet to look into the case. The defendant-respondent No.1 claimed title of the suit property and prayed for release of the property to them. Without reference to the earlier correspondence with Pourashava the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Sylhet observed that he had nothing to do with regard to the right and title in the land and advised the parties to take recourse to the competent Court of law but instructed the requisition authority by his order dated 13-2-1981 to pay rent to Arjya insurance Company which according to him stood amalgamated with defendant-respondent No.1, Sadaran Bima Corporation and directed de-requisition in favour of defendant No.1 which is illegal, ultra-vires, malicious and void and hence the suit. 

 4. The case of the defendant-respondent No. 1 Sadharon Bima Corporation, in brief, is that the suit land was vested to the Crown i.e, the then Government of India free from all encumbrances and when the suit land was in possession of the Government of Assam, it granted lease to Indus-trial Bank Ltd. by a registered bilateral lease deed dated 18-9-1939. The said Industrial Bank constructed permanent two-storied building on the suit land by taking permission from the then Sylhet Municipal Board by improving the condition of land at huge cost and paid rent to the Government and subsequently said Industrial Bank was amalgamated with the Mohalakkshmi Bank by the order of the Hon'ble High Court of Judicature of Fort William of Bengal and on such amalgamation assets for the Industrial Bank vested on the Mohalakkshmi Bank, while Mohalakkshmi Bank is in possession of the suit land, the building and other structures thereon transferred the same to Arjya Insurance Co. Ltd. for consideration of Taka 40,000 by a registered deed dated 23-2-1948, whereupon the Arjya Insurance Co. became exclusive owner and named the said building as Arjya Insurance Building. During Last S/S operation, the suit land and building thereon was recorded in the name of Arjya Insurance Co. as statutory tenant under the Government and records of right had been finally printed and published in the name of Arjya Insurance Company without any objection either by the Sylhet Municipality or anybody else and it is maintained till date. The then Government of East Pakistan for Office accommodation requisitioned the said building from the possession of Arjya Insurance Co. Ltd. In RC Case No. 42/B of 1950-51 and paid monthly rent at the rate of Taka 200 per month to the said company admitting the title and possession of Arjya Insurance Company. In exercising Powers conferred by rule 181 of Defense of Pakistan rule by order dated 11-9-1965 the assets and liabilities of the Arjya Insurance company being unit of Life Insurance Co. of India was vested in Pakistan Insurance Corporation established under Pakistan Insurance Act, 1952 and since then all the assets and Liabilities of all units of the life Insurance Co. Ltd. of India falling within the territory of Pakistan vested in the Insurance Corporation and the said corporation settled many claim of Arjya Insurance Company up to 1971. In 1972 after liberation of Bangladesh the Pakistan Insurance Corporation was renamed as Bangladesh Insurance Corporation under PO No. 18/72 and all assests and liabilities of Pakistan Insurance Corporation falling within Bangladesh Territory vested in Bangladesh insurance Corporation and Subsequently the said corporation was dissolved and vested into Teesta Bima Corporation with all assests and liabilities by PO No. 161 of 1972. Then Sadharan Bima Corporation was constituted and all the assets of Teesta and Kamafully Bima corporation vested in the defendant-respondent No. 1 Sadaron Bima corporation which realizes monthly rents from then allottees of the suit property through the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet with the knowledge of the Pourashava and when the suit property was necessitated for their own use and enjoyment, the Sadaran Bima corporation applied for derequisition of the suit property and the collector is considering the necessity of the Sadaran Bima Corporation passed order on 13-2-1981 favouring derequisition of the suit property in favour of the Sadaran Bima Corporation and, as such, suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 5. The parties led evidence in support of their respective claims. After hearing the trial Court dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiff is not in possession of the suit land while the defendant No. 1 is in possession, who got rent of the suit premises and record of right has been prepared in defendant No. 1's name and without filing suit for recovery of khas possession instant suit is not maintainable; lease was not granted by the Sylhet Pourashava, rather Government of Assam granted lease to the predecessor of the petitioner the defendant No.1 constructed structures in the suit land and as per the provision of section 7 and 8 of the Non-Agricultural and Tenancy Act the plaintiff is not entitled to get possession. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr Chaudhury Morshed Kamal, learned advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1 submits that in lease deed date 18-9-1939 exhibit-1, it was stipulated that after expiry of the period of lease that is for 30 years, the lease shall not be renewed as of right and the lower appellate Court rightly held that the period of lease has been ceased by expiry of time. He next submits that in the subsequent sale deed dated 23-2-1948, exhibit-3 entered into between Mahaiaxmi Bank with Arjya Insurance Company Ltd duration of the original lease has been mentioned for 30 years and, as such, the defendant No.1 cannot claim title to the suit property. He next submits that admittedly the suit property has been acquired for Sylhet Paurashva and during its supersession for two years Assam Government leased out the said property to Sylhet industrial Bank and, as such, after expiry of the lease period, naturally the property reverted back' to the plaintiff and as the government requisitioned the said land for government purposes and, as such, after de-requisition, the plaintiff is entitled to get back the property. He next submits that the defendant No.1 cannot Claim the property by virtue of wrong record of right and, as such, the appellate Court upon consideration of legal aspect as well as facts and circumstances rightly decreed the suit. 

 15. Apart from this if anybody has no title in any property mere record of right will not confer title to him. The trial Court fails to consider the legal provisions and erroneously dismissed the suit. 

 16. The appellate Court on appreciation, of evidence both oral and documentary and also by proper interpretation of documents rightly reversed the judgment of the trial Court and decreed the suit with appreciable reasons and it is settled position of law that if the lower appellate Court reverse any judgment of the trial Court on proper assessment of the evidence on record, it calls for no interference under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 Let a copy of the judgment along with the Lower Court Record be sent to the concern Court.

lawyer:
Md Abdul Awal with Jagadish Chandra Sarker Advocates—For the Appellants. 

Bhabesh Chandra Sarker, DAG—For the Respondents.
parties:
Nipendra Chandra Sarker and others --------- Appellants
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal inter alia is that the instant appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 65 of 2009 in the court of learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka praying for declaration of title and further praying for that the RS khatian No. 4356 in the schedule property was wrongly recorded in the name of government as “হাল সাং ভারত পক্ষে বাংলাদেশ সরকার” and therefore not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 3. The plaintiff's case as stated in the plaint in short is that the schedule suit land originally belonged to one Mohin Chandra Gope who was the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiffs and that he was the CS recorded owner and that his name was recorded in the CS khatian No. 2461, dag No. 425 amounting to a property of 678 decimals of land which was subsequently inherited by his 5 (five) sons. In course of time the property devolved upon the 5 sons of the original CS recorded owner Mohin Chandra Gape. Among the 5 (five) sons 2 (two) were childless. The property, devolved upon the heirs in accordance with the relevant laws. Consequently a nephew being their sister's son named Narayan Chandra Gope inherited the shares of the 2 (two) childless brothers namely Darika Nath Gope and Godadhor Gope in proportion to the amount of his shares accordingly to the applicable law. Another brother Meghu Lal Gope being childless died leaving behind his wife Sreemoti Krishno Dasi Gope as his rightful heir. And the property was proportionally recorded in their names. Ultimately the heirs of the CS recorded owner sold the scheduled suit land through 3 (three) different kabala deeds dated 16-6-1978, 23-5-1978 and 24-5-1978 to Sree Otul Chandra Sarker and the father of the plaintiffs. In pursuance Sree Otul Chandra Sarker and the father of the plaintiffs by dint of the 3 (three) different kabala deeds became owner of 443 decimals of land and accordingly enjoyed possession of the land upon duly mutating “নামজারী ও জমাভাগ), due payment of taxes etc. The VP tohshilder upon examining the documents and the census list issued a statement that the property is not a vested property and is not listed as being such. Meanwhile Sree Otul Chandra Sarker transferred a proportion of his property to his son Omal Chandra Sarker through a registered kabala deed on 16-6-1978. Accordingly Sree Otul Chandra Sarker and Omal Chandra Sarker while holding title and in possession of the property sold 551/4 decimals of land to one Hazi Abdul Samad Sayyal by a registered deed dated 29.06.1983 and on the same date that is 29-6-1983 they sold 551/4 decimals of land to one Abdul Hamid Sayyal by registered deed No. 4510. Subsequently, on 16-8-1983 Abdul Samad Sayyal and Abdul Hamid Sayyal sold their land through 6 (six) several registered deeds to the plaintiffs No. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 respectively. Accordingly the plaintiffs Nos. 1-6 in the present suit became owners of 0.0221 decimals of land by dint of purchase and obtained possession of the same. Accordingly the plaintiffs' father Upendra Chandra Sarker held title and was in possession of 0.0221 decimals of land and his 6 (six) sons were holding title and possession of another 0.0221 decimals of land and while continuing as such the plaintiffs duly completed mutation in their name at the concerned revenue office of the Government by mutation (নামজারী ও জমাভাগ) case No. 2425/84-85 dated 29-1-1985 and accordingly paid taxes being owners of the suit land partly by purchase and partly by inheritance amounting to 0.0442 decimals of land and have been residing in the said land with their families upon constructing house, paying taxes etc. While continuing possession of the suit land the plaintiff No. 1 on 5-1-2009 went to the local office of the AC land for purpose of paying taxes. And thereupon the AC land office informed the plaintiffs that the SA record is duly prepared in their names. But the AC land office however refused to accept taxes since the RS was recorded in the name of the Government. On 5-1-2009 the plaintiffs for the first time discovered that the suit land was wrongly RS recorded in the name of the Government and consequently the addresses of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs were wrongly inserted as “হাল সাং ভারত পক্ষে বাংলাদেশ সরকার” Upon discovery of this wrong record on 5-1-2009 the cause of action to file the suit arose on that date. The plaint further stated that the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiffs had sold the suit land through registered deeds on different dates and the predecessor-in-interest had not left for India prior to the plaintiffs' purchase of the suit land. The plaint also stated that the suit land is not listed in the census list in the name of the Government. And the government was never in possession of such nor did the government ever grant the suit land in lease to any person. The plaint also stated that pursuant to the mutation and the name of the plaintiffs being correctly recorded in the Dhaka City Jorip, the defendants-government filed an appeal under Rule 31 of the Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 before the concerned Assistant Settlement Appeal Officer. Upon hearing of appeal, it was dismissed to the effect that the judgment and order of dismissal of the Appeal consequently went in favour of the plaintiffs and the enlisting of record in the plaintiff's name in the City Jorip was thereby affirmed and which was correctly printed as a gazetted khatian in the Dhaka City Jorip Khatian No. 7203. It was also stated in the plaint that although the wrong recording of the RS record as “হাল সাং ভারত পক্ষে বাংলাদেশ সরকার” which amounts to recording the government of Bangladesh as owner in the suit land, however does not create any impediment in the title and interest of the plaintiffs but yet such wrong R.S record in the name of the government has cast a cloud upon the title of the plaintiffs. And hence the suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-3 entered appearance by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made against them. Defendants inter alia stated in the written statement that the SA recorded owner had left for India during 1965 and they have never transferred the property to any person. The written statement further alleged that the predecessor of the plaintiff's upon collusion and fraudulent means created some forged deed and other documents. They further claimed in the written statement that since the SA record during 1966-1975, the RS recorded owner could not be found anywhere in the country and therefore the suit land was correctly enlisted as a vested property of the government and was correctly recorded in the RS record as “হাল সাং ভারত পক্ষে বাংলাদেশ সরকার”. 

 8. Learned Advocate Mr. Md. Abdul Awal appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs-appellants submits that the trial court upon total non application of mind unjudiciously and incorrectly dismissed the suit. He contends that the trial court failed to consider the several deeds and documents produced before it as exhibits. He contends that inspite of most of the original deeds except 2 (two) as exhibits but even those two being later authenticated by two of the PWs being employees of the registered office, yet the trial court did not even take these material factors into any consideration. He argues that the trial court did not even apply its mind to the fact that the suit land does not appear anywhere in the list of vested property. He elaborates his submission upon assertion that following the appeal under Rule 31 of the Bengal Tenancy Rules the appeal which was made by the defendants-government, before the relevant authority, the Assistant Settlement Appeal officer dismissed the appeal against the defendants and in favour of the plaintiffs followed by the plaintiffs name being correctly recorded in the Dhaka city Jorip upon publication as a gazetted khatian, yet the trial court turned a blind eye to such material factors. He further contends that the trial court did not even consider the deposition made by the PWs and failed to appreciate another material factor that the defendants-government could not produce any documents in support of their claim to title. He reiterates his contention that contrary to the defendants-government's claims as the property being a vested property and in support of their reliance upon the RS being recorded as “হাল সাং ভারত পক্ষে বাংলাদেশ সরকার” however the defendants failed to produce any documents which could even indicate that the suit land is a vested property of the government nor could the defendants show their title to the suit land through any other documents. The learned Advocate further asserts that the trial court arrived upon its finding upon conjecture and surmise and upon non reliance of any material evidence nor did it discuss the deposition made by the PWs. He further continues that the trial court arrived upon a wrong filing that the suit is barred by limitation and dismissed the appeal upon an incorrect finding. Controverting the trial court's finding on the point of limitation he contends that the suit was filed within time in as much as that the cause of action arose on 5-1-2009 when the plaintiff No. 1 went to the A.0 land office and the suit was filed on 15-2-2009. Therefore the suit was filed well within the statutory time. In support of his submissions on the point of limitation he cites two decisions before us one in the case of Bangladesh vs AKM Abdul Hye reported in 56 DLR (AD) 53 and another decision in the case of Abdul Hafez vs Lal Meah reported in 1988 BLD 497. Upon reliance on his assertion and the deposition of the witnesses, evidences placed as exhibits and the other materials on record, he concludes his submissions upon reiteration that the judgment and decree of the trial court does not comprise of legal or factual basis and ought to be set aside and the appeal ought to be allowed for ends of justice. 

 9. Learned DAG Mr. Bhabesh Chandra Sarker opposes the appeal. He however in his submissions failed to show anything from the records or the judgment that could lead to any proof that the property is a vested property of the government or that the government in any manner is the rightful owner of the suit land. He however submits that the trial court correctly dismissed the suit on the point of limitation given that the RS record was prepared as “হাল সাং ভারত পক্ষে বাংলাদেশ সরকার” long before the filing of the suit. 

 10. We have heard the learned Advocates from both sides, perused all materials on records including the judgment of the court below and the deposition of the witnesses from both sides. The plaintiffs produced 23 exhibits which include the kabala deeds and other relevant documents while the defendants failed to produce any documents at all in support of their claims. From perusal of the judgment it transpires that regrettably the trial court did not consider some vital factors which also included the deposition of the PWs. It also transpires that in absence of any documents or any other credible evidence the trial court arrived upon a presumption based on its own conjecture and surmise that the kabala deeds might have been created as a result of "false personation". But however the trial court did not in its finding make any attempt to explain or otherwise analyse the basis of its presumption. 

 11. It is an admitted fact that the CS recorded original owner was Mohin Chandra Gope and upon examination in the various exhibits and the other materials before us it appears that the plaintiffs-appellants before us based their claims to title and possession in the suit land partly by dint of purchase and partly by inheritance mainly relying upon various kabala deeds earlier executed by the predecessors-in-interest and subsequently by the plaintiffs themselves. It is also an admitted fact that the SA record was prepared in the name of the plaintiffs. The trial court in its finding made an observation that 2 (two) of the original deeds were not placed before the trial court by the plaintiffs during trial as exhibits. It observed that the original of 2 deeds being deed No. 22341 dated 23-5-1978 and deed No. 11510 dated 16-6-1978 were not produced before the trial court. But the trial court however ignored or overlooked a vital material factor that the rest of the kabala deeds were produced in its original. Furthermore from the deposition of the PW 4 (record keeper) it appears that the PW 4 has during his deposition certified the authenticity of the deed No. 21268 dated 16-6-1978 including the authenticity of others deeds. The trial court also made an observation that the name of the sister of Darika Nath Gope and Godadhor Gope is not mentioned anywhere in the plaint. We may presume that the trial court evidently made this observation indicating or rather questioning the existence of the nephew Narayan Chandra Gope who was the heir of Dharika Nath Gope and Godha Dhor Gope since they were childless. 

 12. In our opinion the name of the mother of Narayan Chandra Gope being the sister of Dharika Nath Gope and Godha Dhor Gope is not a vital factor for deciding the issues before us since we are here placing our reliance on the various deeds executed by the plaintiffs' predecessor-in-interest which have been produced as exhibits and furthermore we are placing our reliance on the various exhibits produced before the court showing rent receipt, taxes etc. in support of the possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. Furthermore we have noticed that the trial court did not take a relevant fact into consideration which we find necessary to take into consideration to arrive at a correct finding, that being exhibit-7, the certified copy of judgment of the appeal case No. 38110 of 2001 filed under Rule 31 of the Bangal Tenancy Rule, 1955 filed by the defendant before the Assistant Settlement Appeal Officer. It is evident from this decision that the listing of the Dhaka City Jorip was correctly recorded in the name of plaintiff's appellants. Exhibit 7 is the material evidence that the listing of the plaintiff's name in the City Jorip was later affirmed upon appeal. 

 13. We have perused the deposition of the PW 1 being plaintiff No. 2 in the suit. From the deposition of the PW 1 it transpires that he has in his depositions more or less corroborated the statements made in the plaint. Furthermore, he has also referred to the several exhibits in support of his claim including the deeds, namjari, rent receipt, judgment of the appeal case No. 38110 of 2001. PW1 also deposed that the cause of action arose only on 5-1-2009 for the first time upon going to the office of the relevant authorities for the purpose of of payment of taxes. PW1 deposed that on that date the plaintiffs for the first time discovered that the RS was wrongly recorded as “হাল সাং ভারত পক্ষে বাংলাদেশ সরকার”. From the deposition of the PWs 2 and 3 who are kind of neighbours of the plaintiffs, it appears that the deposition of the PWs 2 and 3 are consistent upon the question of possession of the plaintiffs. The PWs 4, 5 and 6 who are the assistant record keepers respectively being government employees, it appears from their deposition that they have authenticated and affirmed the genuinity of the deeds and further positively stated that the various numbers in the volume "(বালাম বই)" and that of the various deeds are the same. We are inclined to opine that the deposition of PWs No. 5 and 6 indicate that there is no inconsistency between the numbers in the list and the deeds pertaining to the suit land and that the deeds are genuine deeds. Conversely DW 1 being land sub-assistant officer of the concerned office deposes that the suit land is a "vested" property and that the original owner left for India many years ago. However the DW 1 failed to produce any documents in support of his claim that the suit land is vested property of the government. Rather in his cross examination he deposes that: “নালিশা জমি সেনসাস তালিকায় আছে কিনা জানা নাই। নালিশা জমির VP দাগ আছে কিনা জানা নাই। সরকার এই জমি লিজ দিয়েছে কিনা বলতে পারবো না।” Such inconsistency between his deposition and the statement upon cross-examination amounts to controverting the defendant's-government's claim to title in the suit land. 

 14. It is also quite clear from the records that no documents whatsoever were produced by the defendants at any stage nor was the suit land ever listed as a vested property. On the other hand it is evident from the record that plaintiffs appellants produced several deeds and other supporting evidences being rent receipts, taxes etc. including several other documents in support of their claim to title and possession. The trial court while basing its finding mainly upon surmise and conjecture however dismissed the suit on the ground of being barred by limitation. But it is our considered finding that from the records and the materials before us, it appears that the cause of action arose on 5-1-2009 when the plaintiff had gone to the concerned local office to pay taxes. 

 15. Learned Advocate for the appellant at one point during his submissions made averments that the cause of action arose only on 5-1-2009 when one of the plaintiffs went to the local tahsil office and for the first time discovered the wrong RS record as “হাল সাং ভারত পক্ষে বাংলাদেশ সরকার” in favour of the defendants-government. Controverting the contention of the defendant-respondent the learned Advocate for the appellant agitates that the suit is not barred by limitation since the cause of action rose on 5-1-2009 and the suit was filed on 15-2-2009 and which is well within time. He further relied upon two decisions, one in the case of Bangladesh vs AKM Abdul Hye reported in 56 DLR (AD) 53. The principle enunciated in that decision of our Apex court is reproduced below: 

 "Against the wrong record-of-rights the person whose interest is affected is required to file the suit seeking declaration of title within six years from the date the person in whose name record has been wrongly prepared and finally published, raises claim on the basis of wrong record." 

 "Suit for declaration of title-Question of starting point for limitation- The plaintiff is not bound to institute a suit for declaration that the entry in the record of rights is wrong —He can wait and sue when invasion on his right is made—Limitation Act (IX of 1908) Article 120". 

 17. We have perused both the decisions and we are in respectful agreement with those including the decision of our Apex court which needless to state is binding upon us. We are inclined to apply the same principle to the case before us and which is relevant for our purpose. We are also of the considered view that the plaintiffs-appellants filed the suit well within time when they first gained knowledge of the invasion into their right. On 5-1-2009 they also learnt that the record has been wrongly prepared and such wrong record gave rise to their cause of action. We are also inclined to observe that the Trial Court's observation and raising doubt on the genuinity of the deeds based on conjecture and surmise and particularly its observation that the deeds were created upon "false impersonation" are inappropriate and unwarranted in as much as that it did not even make any attempt to analyse nor in any other manner tried to explain the basis of its conclusions. Upon an overall appraisal of all materials it is our considered finding that the defendants failed to hopelessly establish their claim with any supporting documentary evidences and their claim of the suit land being "vested" property could not be proved by any supporting evidence. 

 19. Therefore under the facts and circumstances, relying upon the discussions made above and taking into consideration all materials on record before us and the submissions of the learned Counsels, the decisions relied upon and the applicable laws, we find merit in the appeal. 

 Send down the lower court records at once.

8. Mr Md. Omar Farook learned Advocate for the defendant No. 1 petitioner submits that the mortgaged deed dated 4-6-1966 and agreement of reconveyance dated 4-6-1966 (Exhibit-1) became ineffective after sale of the suit land vide kabala dated 17-7-1967 (Exhibit-Ka) and, as such, the plaintiff had no locus-standi to sue for redemption and the suit is not tenable in the eye of law. Mr Omar Farook further submits that the Appellate Court below committed error in not considering the transfer of title of the suit land by the plaintiff which resulted error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate then submits that the plaintiff in his plaint suppressed the transfer of suit land along with other land vide kabala dated 17-6-1967 (exhibit-Ka) and did not challenge the said transfer even after disclosure of the matter by the defendant in the written statement. The defendant No. 1 petitioner proved the sale deed exhibit-Ka by adducing witness DW 2 which was appreciated by the trial Court but the learned appellate Court below failed to consider the evidence of DW 2 about the proof of the said transfer and most illegally opined that the sale deed was not proved according to law as such committed error of law and then he submits that the plaintiff had no subsisting interest over the suit land after execution and registration of sale deed dated 17-6-1967 exhibit-Ka and there was no scope for reconveyance of the suit land in pursuant to mortgage deed and agreement dated 4-6-1966 exhibit-I. The learned Judge of the Court of Appeal below while disposing of the case of redemption failed to determine the issue whether the mortgage was subsisting upto its tenure or not and thus arrived at a contrary findings of fact resulting error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and he then submits that the suit was dismissed on 13-9-1987 and the defendant No. 1 due to necessity took back the sale deed exhibit-Ka from record vide Order No. 49 dated 27-9-1987 but unfortunately the said exhibit-Ka was lost and that the defendant No. I obtained fresh certified copy of mortgage deed dated 4-6-1966 and sale deed dated 17-6-1967 and submitted those before the Appellate Court. Since the certified copy is public document and previously original was marked as exhibit before the trial Court, the appellate Court below, ought to have believe those as valid documents or in the alternative the appellate Court below being a final Court of fact ought to prove its genuineness by calling the volume of the Sub-Registrar Office but without arriving any conclusive proof disbelieving those documents and disbelieving the defendant's case committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The defendant No. 1 after purchase the suit land along with other land vide kabala dated 17-6-1967 transferred the suit land to Ambia Khatun vide kabala dated 17-4-1983 and while dispute arise between the defendant No.1 petitioner and Ambia Khatun, the defendant No. 1 instituted Other Suit No. 145 of 1995 against Ambia Khatun for declaration of title and for permanent injunction which is still pending and during its pendency any proceeding by the trial Court against the same is bad in law. 

 9. Mr Md Shamsul Haque, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties submits that the original deed dated 17-6-1967 was never produced before the Court or any other Authority for mutation, preparation of record-of-rights, payment of revenue etc. and there was no explanation in the written statement as to the where about of the original deed and evidences as regards the missing of the original deed have been apparently untrustworthy. No GD was lodged as regards the missing of the original title deed, even the certified copy of the said deed was taken back without any explanation and was submitted after a long time before this Court only after the police went to the suit-land for execution of the decree of Appellate Court below. The custody of the registered agreement for reconveyance dated 4-6-1966 in original in the hands of the plaintiff-opposite parties herein speaks against the execution of the deed dated 17-6-1967. When the agreement in original was filed in Court by the plaintiff, the defendant No. 1 could not legally satisfy the Court why the agreement in original was not handed over to the defendant No. 1 before registration of the deed dated 17-6-1967. The plaintiff's suit was for redemption of 15 decimal land but the defendants claimed 20 decimal on the strength of the deed dated 17-6-1967 which was straight way denied by the plaintiff, the defendant No. 1 did not prove his possession over the additional 5 decimal of land, no mutation, no record of rights, no payment of revenue of the defendant No. 1 was produced before the Court though the defendant No. 1 claimed that he purchased the said 15 + 05 = 20 decimal of land on 17-6-1967, so it is the conclusive circumstantial proof that the said deed dated 17-6-1967 being a forged deed was never produced by the defendant No. 1 and was never acted upon. Whereas the plaintiff has upto date record of right and up to date payment of revenue as regards the said additional 5 decimal of land, being his paternal property, is the conclusive proof of possession and title of the plaintiff-opposite parties. Mr Haque then submits that the so-called deed dated 17-6-1967 is ex facie a vague one as it does not mention specifically the value of the additional 5 decimals of land and the value of the right of reconveyance while both the instrument required separate stamp and registration cost specifically. Mr Haque further submits that the defendant in depositions and cross-examinations and also at paragraph No. 5 of his/their application for stay of the execution case filed before this Court on 1st day of July, 1998 clearly stated that he has transferred the suit-land to one Ambia Khatun on 17-4-1983 and 11-5-1983 and the plaintiff-opposite parties instituted the suit for redemption on 3-6-1983 and why the defendant No. 1 petitioners is/are fighting the legal battle without impleading said Ambia Khatun and why said Ambia Khatun is not coming for stay of the execution case ? Such contradictory claim and conduct of the defendant petitioners overwhelmingly proves his/their fraud and forgery and thus the plaintiff opposite parties has /have been deprived of the benefit of the suit-land for more than 4 decades. Mr Shamsul Haque then submits that as per section 6(h) of the Transfer of Property Act there can be no transfer to any disqualified transferee. The transferee of the alleged deed dated 17-6-1967 was already a transferee as regards 15 decimals of the suit land as per the registered deed dated 4-6-1966 and therefore he was a disqualified transferee in a deed dated 17-6-1967 where the said 15 decimals of land was in the schedule of both the deeds dated 4-6-1966 and 17-6-1967. The registration of the subsequent deed amounts to cancellation of the earlier deed which is not permitted in law and the sub-registrar was without lawful authority in registering the subsequent deed dated 17-6-1967 and similarly as per section 7 of the Transfer of Property Act only person entitled to transferable property is competent to transfer the said transferable property. While a validly registered deed dated 4-6-1966 was in force and was admitted by the parties, the transferor of the said deed dated 4-6-1966 was already a transferor in respect of 15 decimals of land and he could not be a valid transferor in the deed dated 17-6-1967 where in the schedule the said 15 decimals of land was included. The subsequent deed could not be registered and law cannot be changed by consent of the parties. The subsequent deed in the instant case was simply void, which even does not require a declaration that the said deed is void. Such a deed whenever is produced for any practical purpose would not be accepted and liable to be impounded by any lawful authority and as per section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act an ostensible owner can transfer any property. Now as per the deed dated 4-6-1966 the defendant was ostensible owner and the defendant could sell the suit land, then how a person entitled to sell could buy the same suit land from a person who is already a transferor and at the later time he had no title no interest in the suit land. Until his right to reconveyance was specifically enforced and the suit land was transferred back to him by a registered deed, he had no right, title and interest on 17-6-1967 over the suit land and he could not execute the subsequent deed as regards the 15 decimal of land. Mr Haque then submits that as per section 4 of the Stamp Act, 1899 additional stamp is required for additional instrument. Obviously the alleged deed dated 17-6-1967 had additional instrument, however no consideration was specified for the additional instrument, namely the right of reconveyance, and, as such, no separate stamp was used and no registration cost was paid and it was also not clear what was the consideration for the additional 5 decimals of land. As per section 14 there can be no second instrument on same stamp paper and section 15 of the said Act provides that such deed is deemed as unstamped which is liable to be impounded whenever it is produced, and sections 27, 33, 35, 43, 57, 61(4), 62, taken together the said deed was liable to be impounded, not admissible in evidence and the person in possessesion of such a deed is liable for criminal action as per the Stamp Act and then submits that as per Schedule 1(55) of the Stamp Act, 1999 the right of reconveyance could be released or renounced as per law upon payment of specified stamp duty but the defendant No. 1 had arranger for registration of a forged deed dated 17-6-1967 which was if registered at all was registered illegally and that is an invalid document which can never be acted upon and has been acted upon in the last about 50 years and as per the Registration Act once sale deed is registered, the same cannot be cancelled by consent or by subsequent deed (AIR 2011 Mad 66 FB), and a sale deed once registered can be avoided only by a subsequent registered document transfer (27 CWN 8 PC) and then submits that as per section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with the decisions reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237, 66 DLR (AD) 162, 20 BLC (AD) 4 the plaintiff-opposite party is entitled to recover possession of the 15 decimal of the suit land. Mr Haque then submits the plaintiffs case stands proved by admission of the defendant No. 1 and the defendant's case being denied by the plaintiff, the Evidence Act provides onus upon the defendant to prove his case, because in the absence of any evidence in this case the plaintiff is entitled to the decree in his favour inasmuch as the plaintiffs case has been admitted by the defendant and the plaintiff acquired title by operation of law and the Appellate Court below findings as regards burden of proof is in accordance with law and the trial Court erred in law as regards onus of proof and thus the Rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his contentions he has referred to the case of Emmanuele Grech vs Antonio Grech, reported in 6 DLR 599 case of Haji Waziullah vs Additional Deputy Commissioner, reported in 41 DLR 96, case of Amirun Nessa vs Golam Kashem reported in 42 DLR 499, case of Abdul Hamid vs Dr Sadeque Ali reported in 27 DLR 511, case of Abdul Quddus vs Anjuman Khatoon reported in 36 DLR 313, case of Abu Bakkar vs Nazir Ahmed reported in 34 DLR 239, case of Shaukat Ali vs Shamsum Bibi reported in 27 DLR 59. Mr Haque lastly submits that in the instant case the transaction i.e. the usufructuary mortgage began on 4-6-1966 and after 7 years on 4-6-1974 the term of usufructuary mortgage (খায় খালাসী বন্ধক) expired. So the transaction was alive when the President Order No. 88 of 1972 was promulgated. So the President Order No. 88 of 1972 and the provision of Section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 are applicable on this transaction as it was alive up to 1974. So the President Order No. 88 of 1972 and provision of section 95A, the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 should apply in this case and the Rule in the instant civil revision is liable to be discharged for end of justice with exemplary cost as the defendant deprived the plaintiff opposite party herein for a period of more then 4 decades. The defendant failed to prove his case by adducing oral and documentary evidence and the learned trial Court was unable to realize the legal issues involved in the suit as such committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice but the Appellate Court below rightly passed the judgment and decree on the basis of evidence and considering the legal issues. 

 10. Heard defendant No. opposite parties the learned Advocates for the I petitioners and the plaintiff-and perused the record. 

 11. The plaintiff for want of money mortgaged he suit land to the defendant No. 1 taking Taka 375 as loan and handed over possession of the mortgaged and in favour of the defendant with the understanding that the suit land will reconvey to the plaintiff if he can pay the loan money within 8 years. Accordingly, the defendant No. 1 executed a registered agreement in favour of the plaintiff on the same day. The defendant No. 1 in connivance with the defendant No. 2 abstained from retransferring the suit land and enjoying the suit land after expiry of 8 years and hence the suit. The defendant No. 1 congested the suit and claimed that he purchased the suit land vide registered kabala dated 4-6-1966 and executed an agreement in favour of the plaintiff and subsequently the plaintiff due to economic crisis sold the suit land to him (defendant) along with other land vide registered kabala dated 17-6-1967. The said original deed 17-6-1967 was never produced before the Court and there was no explanation in this regard and on the other hand, the registered agreement for reconveyance dated 4-6-1966 in original in the hands of the plaintiff which speaks against the execution of the aforesaid deed dated 17-6-1967 and the defendant failed to prove that the said deed dated 17-7-.1967 was executed by the plaintiff. On the basis of the said deed dated 17-56-1967 the defendant claimed 20 decimal land but failed to prove his possession over the entire land and no mutation, no record of right and no payment of revenue of entire 20 decimal land was produced before the Court which indicates that the said deed was never acted upon. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on, record I find no substance in the Rule.

full_judgment:
"From the materials on record as discussed hereinbefore, it is evident that the petitioner's predecessor himself never claimed personal right, title or ownership to the disputed land/property. Rather, he himself filed a suit before the court as President of Anjuman -E-Ittehad Bangladesh and in that suit also it was decided that late Hazrat Moulana Pir Abdul Jabbar does not claim the disputed land/property as his personal property. Curiously enough, the heirs of Late Hazrat Moulana Pir Abdul Jabbar, who stepped into the shoes of late Hazrat Moulana Pir Abdul Jabbar are now claiming title to the dispute land by filing Other Class Suit No. 97 of 2007 as heirs of Late Hazrat Moulana Peer Abdul Jabbar. Late Hazrat Moulana Abdul Jabbar himself claimed that the disputed land/property belongs to Anjuman-E-Ittehad. Be that as it may, it transpires that earlier the same impugned order was challenged by the petitioner in Writ Petition No.672 of 2007 and on the date of pronouncement of judgment, the Rule in the said writ petition was discharged for non-prosecution. But the petitioner once again has challenged the same impugned Memo and sought for the same direction upon the respondents with the same grounds. The act of the petitioner unwarranted. Before declaration of the petitioner's title to the disputed land/property, the petitioner cannot be said to be a person aggrieved", as from the judgment of Other Class Suit No.77 of 1991. It transpires that petitioner's predecessor-in-interest never claimed the disputed land/property as his personal property. 

 8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel; for the petitioner, has submitted that in deciding the property of the impugned Memo challenged before it, the High Court Division failed to consider that the Ministry had no locus standi to issue such order either to the Deputy Commissioner or to the concerned Revenue Officer directing them to accept rent in respect of the disputed land from writ-respondent no.6. He has further submitted that the question of accepting rent would arise only when an immovable property is recorded in the name of someone and admittedly the disputed land is recorded in the name of the writ-petitioners predecessor; the High Court Division erred in law in discharging the Rule and as such, the impugned judgment and order calls for interference by this Court. 

 10. We have looked into the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950). We have found no provision therein which authorised the Ministry/the Government through any Ministry to direct the Revenue Officer to accept rent from a particular person. From the impugned judgment, it appears that the High Court Division failed to give its attention to this legal aspect of the case. Procedures as to the maintenance and revisions of the record of rights have been laid down in Chapter XVII of the Act, 1950 and the Rules framed thereunder vide State Acquisition Rules, 1955 and as per the provisions incorporated therein, one has to apply to the concerned Revenue Officer for mutation of his/its name and if such prayer is allowed then and then only the question of accepting rent from that person would arise, but in the instant case, it does not appear that writ-respondent No.6 or anyone on its behalf ever filed any application to the concerned authority for mutation of its name or record its name in the record of rights and accept rent. Therefore, the impugned Memo issued by the Ministry of Land was passed without any sanction of law and as such, the same cannot be sustained. However, we are of the view that writ respondent No.6 if so advised, may file proper application before the appropriate authority to mutate or record its name and if such application is filed, the concerned authority shall consider the same in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Act, 1950 and the rules of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 and any party including the writ-petitioners shall have the opportunity to raise legal objection, if any, and the concerned authority shall decide the matter on the basis of the materials produced before it, 

 12. The impugned Memo and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division are set aside. If so advised, writ -respondent No.6 may file a proper application before the appropriate authority for mutating /recording its name and if such application is filed, the concerned authority shall consider and dispose the same in accordance with the law.

Chowdhury claiming ownership of 35 decimal of land filed objection Case No. 650 under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 against the khatian prevailing in the name of the petitioner and his co-sharers and the said objection case was heard analogously with objection case No. 651 filed by said Anisur Rahman Chowdhury and both objection case No. 650 and 651 were rejected on 24-11-1997 for want of the applicant's title and possession against which said Anisur Rahman filed Appeal No. 2656 of 1998 under Rule 31 and simultaneously filed Appeal No. 2655 of 1998 against BS (DP) khatian No. 1138 in the names of the heirs of Shamsul Huq Chowdhury and both the appeals were dismissed by the judgment and order dated 14-10-2001 and the appellate authority observed that-আপীলকারী পক্ষ ১৯৪২ সনের একটি দলিল মূলে নালিশী সাবেক ২৮০৭ এবং ২৮১০ দাগের ১১৮ শতক মধ্যে ৩৫ শতক ভূমি দাবী করেন। আপীলকারী পক্ষের উক্ত দলিলের দাতাগণের নাম বা দাতাগণের মাতার নাম সি,এস রেকর্ডে নাই এবং এস,এ,রেকর্ডেও নাই। ১৯৪২ সনের দলিল মূলে জমিদারী সেরেস্তায় কোন নাম জারী হয় নাই। SA & T Act 1950 এর 19(2) ধারা অনুযায়ী আপীলকারী পক্ষ এস,এ রেকর্ড সংশোধনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করেন নাই। উক্ত Act এর 143(A) ধারার সুযোগও আপীলকারী পক্ষ গ্রহণ করেন নাই। আপীলকারী পক্ষ দেওয়ানী আদালতে কোন স্বত্ব মোকদ্দমা করেন নাই। and the appellate authority further affirmed the findings of the objection officer which was observed as “উভয় আপত্তি কেসের পক্ষগণের বক্তব্য, কাগজপত্র, সার্ভেয়ার ও উপসহকারী সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসারের তদন্ত রিপোর্ট ইত্যাদি পর্যালোচনাক্রমে দেখা যায় বাদীপক্ষ ২১-২-৮২ তারিখের ৬১২ নং দলিল মূলে সি এস রেকর্ড বহির্ভূত মালিক হইতে খরিদ করেন। কিন্তু SA  রেকর্ড করাইতে পারেন নাই এবং রেকর্ড সংশোধনের পদক্ষেপ নেন নাই। তাছাড়া সার্ভেয়ার, সাব এস,এস, ও-এর তদন্ত রিপোর্টে বাদীপক্ষেও দখল আছে মর্মে সুষ্পষ্ট রিপোর্ট পাওয়া যায় নাই। অন্যদিকে বিবাদীপক্ষ CS এবং SA রেকর্ড এবং মাননীয় মুনসেফী আদালত ফেনীর TS No.1366/1926 এর আদেশ মোতাবেক বিবাদীপক্ষেও নাম সঠিকভাবে প্রস্তুত হইয়াছে মনে করি।” that it is stated that the petitioner along- with other co-sharers filed objection case No. 235 for correction of sketch Map which was rejected against which appeal No. 5211 of 2001 under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 was preferred before by the order dated 13-5-2002 directing the Surveyor to hold local investigation and to submit report to that effect; that on 3-6-2002 the appellate author- ity took up the appeal for hearing and examined the Badar investigation report which was made a part of the Judgment as the parties did not express discenting view and the appellate authority by the order dated 3-6-2002 allowed the appeal with correction of Sketch Map as prayed for in holding that “সাবেক ২৮০৭ ও ২৮১০ দাগের হাল ৫৩১০ দাগ এরিয়া ১.১৮ একরের তদন্ত রিপোর্টে দেখা যায় আপীলকারীপক্ষ উক্ত দাগের উত্তরাংশে ৪২ ডিং সর্ব দক্ষিণাংশে ৪৬ ডিং এবং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষ মধ্যাংশে ৩০ ডিং দখল করিতেছে। যাহা শুনানীকালে পক্ষ স্বীকার করেন।..................উভয়পক্ষের স্বীকৃত মতে সাবএ,এস,ও কর্তৃক প্রস্তুতকৃত বদর প্রতিবেদন মোতাবেক আপীলকারীপক্ষের দাবী মঞ্জুরক্রমে বিরোধীয় হাল ৫৩১০ দাগের ৪২ ডিং ও ৫৩১০/৫৪৫৮ দাগের ৪৬ ডিং একুনে ৮৮ ডিং ডিপি ১১৩৮ নং খতিয়ানে বহাল রহিয়া এবং প্রতিবাদী হাল দাগ ৫৩১০/৫৪৫৮ দাগ এরিয়া ৩০ শতক বহাল রাখিয়া প্রতিবাদীর ডিপি ১১৩৮  খতিয়ানে রেকর্ড করিয়া আনুষঙ্গিক সংশোধন করা হয় এবং বদর ফি বাজেয়াপ্ত করা হইল।" that it is stated that after dismissal of appeal Nos. 2656 of 1998 and 2655 of 1998 on 14-10-2001 by the order passed by Assistant Settlement Officer, Land Record and Survey Directorate, Tejgaon, Dhaka, the record of rights remained in the names of the petitioner and his co-sharers on the basis of earlier SA khatian and they have been possessing peacefully with the knowledge of all including the respondent No.9 since their predecessor-in-interest and the Judgment of the Appeal Nos. 2656 and 2655 of 1998 remained in force on the Appellant of those Appeals did not proceed to the higher forum as per provision of section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act rather recently the respondent No.9 accompanied with some persons tried to disturb the possession of the petitioner and while the petitioner raised objection the respondent No. 9 claimed possession as per note in the remark column of BS (DP) khatian No. 11 24 in such way হাল ৫৩১০/৫৪৫৮ দাগে দক্ষিণঅংশেখরিদ সূত্রে ভোগদখল ২৮ র্ডিং ১৩৯৮ বাংলা সন হইতে আনিছুর রহমান চৌধুরী পিং আরিফুর রহমান চৌধুরী" which will be evident from Annexure-C to this writ petition; that it is stated that on the basis of claim of the respondent No.9 the Petitioner upon further query came to know about the order dated 17-5-2003 of the respondent No.6 in pursuance of the order dated 19-2-2003 of the respondent No.5, the Memo No. 5/94/3 102/1 dated 18-12-2002 of the respondent No.3 and the 'Secret Enquiry Report' dated 16-7- 2002 held at the instance of the respondent Nos. 4-7 by which the note regarding possession of the respondent No. 9 in the Remark Column of BS (DP) khatian No. 1124 was made although the said khatian remained in the names of the Northern portion and 48 decimal in Southern portion of plot No. 5310 but the respondent No. 9 beyond the knowledge of the petitioner arranged a 'Secret Inquiry Report and in collusion with respondent Nos. 3, 4-7 and 9 succeeded to make entry of possession with comment that he has been possessing 28 decimal since 1398 BS which correspondence to 1991 AD but in 1997 in con testing objection cases under Rule 30 and Appeals under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 the respondent No. 9 Anisur Rahman Chowdhury did not raise that by purchase he has been possessing 28 decimal of land infringed the fundamental rights of the petitioner as guaranteed under Articles 27, 31 of the Constitution, as such, the act done by the respondent Nos. 3, 4, 5 and 6 are liable to be declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, the respondent No.8 dismissed the Appeal Case No. 2655/98 and 2656/98 holding the possession of the petitioner and his co-sharers over 88 decimal as per decree dated 19-9-1927 in Partition Suit No. 1366 of 1926 and further the respondent No. 7 found possession of the petitioner and his co- sharers over 88 decimal of plot No. 5310 in holding Local Investigation in Appeal Case No. 5211 of 2001, but unfortunately the respondent No.7 was present while the respondent No. 4 held Secret Inquiry illegally and the said respondent No.7 abated the biased act of the respondent No. 4 divulging the criminal intention and misused the power and liability of a Public Officer in from of making wrong entry of another person without legal basis in the Record of Right of a law abiding citizen and this petitioner prays before your lordships to take into account such types of misconduct of a Public Officer in handling the right of citizens over their properties as conferred under Article 42(1) of the constitution as those are without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that as soon as the petitioner came to know about the impugned orders served a notice demanding notice through his lawyer but yet received no reply or any positive act in rescinding the impugned orders; that that the petitioner was not aware of the acts done by the respondents through impugned Memo and orders and when came to know about the said orders, the period of limitation as provided under section 148 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has already been expired and the petitioner was no other efficacious alternative forum, but to file this writ petition. 

 4. Learned Advocate Mr Khurshid Alam Khan appearing for the petitioner, first of all, submits that he has been instructed by the learned Advocates Mrs. Shahanara Begum and Mr Md Aziz Taufique to conduct hearing of this matter as a senior friend. He has next drawn our attention to an order dated 13.9.2001 and to paragraph No. 17 of the said order (Annexure- D1) and submits that said order was signed on 14-10-2001, by the Assistant Settlement Officer, who has disposed of 2 appeals, i.e. Appeal No. 2655 of 1998, against which Objection Case No. 651 dated 24-4-1997 and another Appeal No. 2656 of 1998, against which Objection Case No. 650 dated 24-11-2097, were filed. He next submits that, both Objection Miscellaneous Cases were filed under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 and the said two objection cases having been decided against the petitioner-appellants, they have preferred the aforesaid two appeals under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955. He further submits that the aforesaid two appeals, being No. 2655 of 1998 and 2656 of 1998, both under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955, were decided against the appellants, vide the judgment and order dated 14.10.2001, which is well reasoned and all the relevant facts have been detailed in the said judgment as well as the decision of the superior court has been referred to by the appellate authority. Besides cases of both the sides, the appellants and the respondents, has also been stated and discussed in the judgments preferred under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955. The learned Advocate next submits that it has been recorded in the said judgment (Annexure- D 1) that the appellants side under Rule 31 (respondent No. 9 in this matter) has purchased the suit land by a Kabala deed No. 612 dated 21- 12-42 from the person who is not CS recorded owner and could not get their name recorded in SA Khatian. The appellate authority, under Rule 31, has further recorded in his judgment that the CS and SA record were prepared in the name of the respondents i.e. the writ petitioners in this matter, pursuant to judgment passed by the then Munsif Court, Feni, in Title Suit No. 1366 of 1926 and that the writ petitioner is representing the interest of other writ petitioners (respondents in appeal filed under Rule 31) as one of the family members. He also submits that after bare elaborate discussion of the facts and circumstances of the case of the parties and narrating facts as well as the circumstances of the case of both the sides and then having considered all material facts and documents along with the decisions of the higher court and the concerned law, the aforesaid judgment were passed in Appeal Nos. 2655 of 1998 and 2656 of 1998, both filed under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 and were heard and disposed of analogously, whereby both the appeals were disallowed. In this situation and in the light of the background, facts and circumstances of this case, the learned Advocate emphatically submits, that the impugned orders dated 17- 5-2003, 19-2-2003,18-12-2002 and the impugned secret enquiry dated 16-7-2002 and making entry of possession in the name of the respondent No.9, Anisur Rahman Chowdhury, Son of Late Alhaj Arifur Rahman Chowdhury, who was one of the appellants in the column NO.9 of the concerned Kabuliat, as possessors is totally without jurisdiction, ultra vires and is of no legal effect and all the impugned orders along with said direction is liable to be struck down. In support of his contention challenging the impugned orders, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that, after final disposal of the aforesaid 2 appeals filed under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955, the respondent No.3 had no authority or jurisdiction, what so ever, to entertain any application filed by Anisur Rahman Chowdhury and others or to pass the impugned orders (Annexures- E, E1, E2 and E3) after the final order was passed and signed on 14-10-2001, by the appellate authority, under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 i.e. the Assistant Settlement Officer (Annexure-D 1). He also submits that in the impugned orders the respondent No.3 has admitted that he has taken up the matter ex-parte for disposal. On this point the learned Advocate asserts that, 'but it has been recorded in the impugned order that the notice has been served upon the other side. Admittedly no notice was served the matter was heard ex-parte by the respondent No. 3 and there is no materials on record to show that any notice had been served before passing the impugned order and the entire proceedings, impugned before this court as well as the impugned orders were passed behind the back of the petitioner and secretly in connivance with the respondent No. 9 (Anisur Rahman Chowdhury) and others, the learned Advocate adds. The learned Advocate further submits that, it shows malafide on the part' of the respondent No. 3. Besides, he also submits, that the impugned order passed by the respondent No.3 is not supported by any materials on record, although the impugned orders are beyond the authority inasmuch as the appellate authority has disposed of both the appeals under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955. The case of the petitioner has neither been controverted nor been denied by any of the respondents by filing any affidavit-in-opposition. 

 8. We find that the respondent No.9, filed objections under Rule 31 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 to record the suit land in their names, but his two objections being rejected, he had preferred two Appeals, numbered 2655 of 1998 and 2656 of 1998, against the said Objection Case Nos. 650 and 651. 

 10. We respectfully agree with the above quoted ratio of judgment and order, reported in 65 DLR 168 Passed by a Bench of this Division. We have also considered the application of the learned Advocate with the impugned order and the proceedings drawn by the respondent No. 4 and filed by the respondent No.9. We having consulted Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, find that the respondent No. 3 had no jurisdiction to entertain such an application either by way of review or sitting as a court of appeal. Besides the finding recorded in the impugned order is not supported by any materials on record, although we did have to not enter into the merit of the impugned orders inasmuch as it is without jurisdiction and in 44 DLR (AD) 260 it has been held that, jurisdiction of a court goes to the very root of a matter brought before it, and if a court got no jurisdiction everything shall fall through. In the facts and circumstances of this case and the materials on record before, we are of the further view, that the impugned orders are malafide too. Accordingly, we find merit in this rule and the same is to be made absolute with ancillary directions.

 3. The defendant No. 33 Bashir Miah, having entered appearance contested the suit upon filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia and Bama Charan Paul and his three brothers having been in possession of the suit land settled an area of 2.08 acres of land in favour of the defendants upon obtaining salami from them fixing annual rent, by way of a korfa settlement, thereafter upon request from the defendant No. 33, Bama Charan Paul and his three brothers granted amalnama in favour of the defendant No. 33 in respect of an area of 2.08 acres out of the said CS Khatian on 6-9-46 and possession was accordingly handed over there-after the answering defendant carried on possession over the same upon payment of rent to the Zaminders obtaining receipt and he has been in possession of his purchased land upon growing paddy and enjoying usufructs there-from ever since 6-9-46, the date on which the amalnama was executed in his favour by Bama Charan and his three brothers; the defendant.  17. In the case of Gopal Das Soni vs Government of Bangladesh, 13 BLC (AD) 69, it has been held, it is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the land in suit being the land within periphery of Khulna Hat and Bazar, compensation roll has been prepared and finally published in the gazette and that being the undisputed fact relief sought in the suit was not available to the plaintiffs so long compensation roll is not revised and the land is being shown as retainable class of land. It is also seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that compensation roll in respect of the land in suit was prepared as back as in 1962 upon assessing considerable amount of money and thereupon compensation roll has been published in the gazette. It is further seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that a sketch map has been prepared some time in 1975 by the Government in respect of the land in suit and the same has been shown within the periphery of the Khulna Hat and Bazar. The High Court Division On consideration of the materials on record, particularly the fact of preparation of compensation assessment roll and publication thereof in the gazette as well as the sketch map prepared in 1975 showing the land in suit within the periphery of Khulna Hat and Bazar set aside the judgment and decree of the courts below. The learned Counsel has sub-mitted that compensation assessment roll in respect of the land of the plaintiffs and publication thereof was illegal and that publication of the said illegal assessment roll can no way take away the title of the plaintiffs in the land which is of retainable class of land and that also not within the periphery of Khulna Hat and Bazar. He has also submitted that the sketch map said to have been prepared in' 1975 showing land within periphery of Khulna Hat and Bazar is an unauthorised and illegal act of the respondents and, on the basis thereof plaintiffs cannot be deprived of their tenanted land which they are legally entitled to retain. The 'submission of the learned Counsel as of no merit since preparation of the Compensation assessment roll and the publication thereof has the' legal presumption that the land claimed by the plaintiffs is of non-retainable class of land and that as on the publication of the condensation assessment roll in the gazette, the land has vested in the Government the plaintiffs " are not entitled to raise 'any claim in the land and as such, relief sought in the suit was not available to them. Moreover, as back as in 1975, the Government prepared the sketch map showing the land in suit within the periphery 'of Khulna Hat and. Bazar and that as it appears the said sketch map has been prepared in the background of the publication of the Compensation assessment roll in the gazette the same carries legal weight in arriving at the decision as to' the class of land in suit. As in the background of the materials on record the High Court Division has arrived at the finding the Courts below were in error in decreeing the suit, in our view, the finding so arrived at by the High' . Court Division is in accordance with law and suffers from infirmity and illegality. 

 19. In the case of Anwara Begum Chowdhurani vs Nur Jahan Begum, 27 DLR (AD) 109, it has been held; it appears that mention of the different classes of tenants or occupants has been made in the above quoted provisions of law. It was argued that sub-section (1) of section 24 of the Act clearly indicates that no under raiyati holding would remain in existence at the time of the preparation of the record-of-rights which would be subsequent to the Notification under section 3 of the Act. Rule 18 provides for the preparation or revision of the record-of-rights on the basis of which the compensation Assessment-roll would be pre-pared and published and rule 61 says that the different classes of tenancies would cease to exist with publication of the Notification under section 3 of the Act and that entire chain of interests of rent-receivers would be eliminated only after the publication of the Compensation Assessment roll. Thereafter a Notification would be published under sub-section (2) of section 43 declaring that the compensation assessment-roll in respect of that area had been finally published and after this publication of Notification, the whole of Part V of the Act would come into operation. The sum and sub-stance of the contention of the learned Counsel is that raiyati interest did not cease to exist and that under-raiyat was not upgraded before Part V came into operation. With a view to strengthen his argument the learned Counsel relied on a decision in Afran Ali Sheikh's case reported in 14 DLR (Dacca) 791. It is a Single Bench decision by Idris, J, of the Dacca High Court. The said case was under section 26F of the BT Act. In that case the question arose as to whether there was an automatic elevation of under-raiyats to the status of raiyats with effect from 14-4-56 when all rent-receiving interests vested in the Government. The learned Judge held that publication of Notification under section 3 of the act did not eliminate the different classes of tenancies till publication of the compensation assessment-roll, i.e., till Part V of the act came into operation. In coming to that decision Idris, J., it appears, relied on an unreported decision by Asir, J., in Civil Revision Case Nos.1129 and 1130 of 1960 of the Dacca High Court. On the authority of the decision of Idris, J and the pro-visions of law referred to above the learned Counsel submitted that pre-emption was not available in the present case to an under raiyati even if he had occupancy right'.

full_judgment:
4. The petitioner as pre-emptee contested the Miscellaneous Case by filing written objection denying all the material allegations made in the application contending, inter alia, that the case is barred for defect of parties; that the land under pre-emption was shown as under valued; that she is widow and poor; that her father Jagabandhu Saha was the CS recorded tenant of the land; that she and her mother Haridashi Saha inherited the property of her father; that the title of her mother Haridasi Saha was declared in Title Suit No. 125 of 1989; and that the Miscellaneous Case is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mrs Promila Biswas, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, supports the Rule and submits that the Miscellaneous Case for pre-emption is barred for defect of parties, inasmuch as her father Jagabandhu was the original CS recorded tenant of the land and she and her mother inherited his property but her mother Haridasi was not made party. She adds that the learned Judges of the Courts below failed to consider that the land under pre-emption was the agricultural land and amalgamation of agricultural and non agricultural plots of lands in CS khatians all the plots in that khatian take the status of agricultural land and, as such, the instant application ought to have been filed under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The learned Counsel lastly submits that the learned Judges of the Courts below failed to weigh and sift the evidence on record as required by law and evidently fell in an error in coming to his ultimate decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 9. Mr Goutam Kumar Roy, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1, opposes the Rule by filing a counter-affidavit and submits that the pre-emptor is the co-sharer by purchase of the case khatian but the pre-emptee is the stranger to the land under pre-emption. He adds that the pre-emption right is the statutory right and the case has been filed within time and considering the evidence on record both the Courts below concurrently allowed the application for pre-emption. The learned Counsel adds that all the co-sharers of SA Khatians were made parties, so the Miscellaneous Case is not barred for defect of parties. He lastly submits that the judgments and orders of the Courts below are based on concurrent finding of facts. So, such findings should not be disturbed. In support of his contention the learned Counsel refers the case of Fatema Bibi vs Sree Manik Lal Somaddar and others reported in 50 DLR (AD) 97. Therein it is held— 

 Concurrent findings of fact are not generally disturbed by the High Court Division exercising revisional jurisdiction. But when the two courts below failed to consider some important documentary evidence and findings of facts arrived at by them are not based on materials on record, the High Court Division may be justified in interfering with the concurrent findings of fact on giving cogent reasons." 

 12. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Counsels of both sides, I have gone through the revisional application, application for pre-emption, written objection, deposition of the witnesses, all exhibits, judgments and orders of the Courts below, other materials on record and given my anxious consideration to the sub-missions advanced by the learned Counsels of both sides. 

 14. I find from the evidence on record that the pre-emptor is the co-sharer by purchase of the khatian under pre-emption as described in SA Khatian No. 2572 of Plot No. 134. The vendor (opposite party No. 2) transferred the land under pre-emption to the pre-emptee (herein petitioner) by a registered kabala deed dated 30-4-1995 (Exhibit-2) and the plaintiff filed the application for pre-emption on 20-5-1995 i.e. within time. 

 15. On careful scrutiny of SA record of rights (Exhibit 1), it appears that the name of Haridasi, mother of pre-emptee, is not there, so she is not a necessary party Moreover, she is not co-sharer by inheritance, inasmuch as at the time of preparation of SA record of rights the Khatians were separated. 

 17. It appears that the findings arrived at by the Courts below having been rested upon consideration and discussion of legal evidence and materials on record and also on a correct and proper analysis of the legal aspects involved in the case and the findings being findings of fact are not liable to be disturbed by the High Court Division in exercise of power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 "A provisional court acts beyond its jurisdiction in setting aside concurrent finding of fact, when there is no misreading and mis-appreciation  of the evidence on record. " 

 21. Having regard to the facts, I find that all the issues involved in the case have rightly been framed, considered and decided by the trial Court with reference to the evidence and materials on record. Moreover, I do not find any misreading or non consideration of the evidence on record. The impugned judgment and order passed by the Court of appeal below are well reasoned backed by sufficient oral and documentary evidence, which cannot be interfered. Therefore, I failed to discover any merit in the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioner. On the contrary the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the opposite party No. 1 prevails and appears to have a good deal of force. 

 Send down the lower Court's record at once with a copy of judgment for information and for taking necessary action.
